questions.stem: Given the class structure shown below, which types of CIs will be included in a report run against the cmdb_ci_computer table?

options.text: Just CIs defined directly in cmdb_ci_computer
CIs defined directly in cmdb_ci_computer and all parent classes
CIs defined directly in cmdb_ci_computer and all child classes

questions.explanation: The image shows the CMDB class hierarchy: cmdb > cmdb_ci > cmdb_ci_hardware > cmdb_ci_computer, with child classes cmdb_ci_server (which further extends to cmdb_ci_win_server, cmdb_ci_linux_server, cmdb_ci_unix_server) and cmdb_ci_pc_hardware. Reports run against a table include records from that table AND all child (extended) tables. A report on cmdb_ci_computer returns CIs from the table itself plus all classes that extend it (server types, pc_hardware). Parent classes like cmdb_ci or cmdb_ci_hardware are NOT included — inheritance flows downward only (C).

questions.stem: Which field from the configuration item will automatically populate in the Assignment group field of an incident record?
questions.explanation: The Support group field on a CI record automatically populates the Assignment group field on an incident. The baseline business rule 'Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO' checks the CI's Support group first; if empty, it falls back to the Support group on the associated Service Offering. Managed by (A), Approval group (C), and Change group (D) are not used for incident assignment population.

questions.stem: Which of the following are defined for a given change model? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: A change model defines: State model (B) which specifies available states, State transitions (E) which define allowed movement between states, and State transition conditions (C) which set prerequisites for each transition (e.g., required fields). Phase transitions (A) and Phase model (D) are not components of change models — change management uses states, not phases.

questions.stem: When is a change task for Post Implementation Review created for an unauthorized change?

options.text: When the change request moves to Close
When a change manager accepts the change
When the change request moves to a state of Review
When the change request moves to a state of Assess

questions.explanation: The Post Implementation Review (PIR) change task is created when the change request moves to the Review state (C). The Review state is specifically designed for post-implementation review activities. This is handled by the Change - Emergency - Review or Change - Normal flow. It's not created at Close (A), acceptance (B), or Assess (D).

questions.stem: Which should be used to explore the entire hierarchy and table definitions of the Configuration Management Database Classes?
questions.explanation: The CI Class Manager (B) is the tool for exploring the complete hierarchy and table definitions of CMDB classes. It shows parent/child class relationships, attributes, and table structure in a visual tree. Reports (A) display data, not schema. Application Menus (C) manage navigation. Dependency View (D) shows CI relationships, not class hierarchy.

questions.stem: Which of the following cannot be defined or set through a Catalog UI Policy?

options.text: Apply a requirement to all form views
Setting a catalog category to visible

questions.explanation: Catalog UI Policies cannot apply requirements to all form views (B) — they apply only to the Service Catalog form context, not platform form views. Catalog UI Policies CAN set variables to mandatory (A), set catalog categories to visible (C), and set variables to read-only (D). The 'all form views' scope is a platform UI Policy capability, not a Catalog UI Policy one.

questions.stem: Which type of catalog item should be used to create an incident record from the portal?
questions.explanation: A Record Producer (D) creates records in a specified target table from the Service Catalog. To generate an incident from the portal, you configure a Record Producer with the Incident table as the target. Catalog Items (C) create Requested Items, not incidents. Order Guides (C) bundle multiple items. Incident Template (A) is not a catalog item type.

questions.stem: Which incident management roles are activated by installing the ITSM Roles plugin (com.snc.itsm.roles)? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The ITSM Roles plugin (com.snc.itsm.roles) provides granular read/write roles. For incidents, it creates sn_incident_read (A) for view-only access and sn_incident_write (D) for edit access. These complement the base itil role with finer control. Options B and E (itsm_incident_*) are not the actual role names. incident_manager (C) exists but isn't created by this plugin.

questions.stem:
A customer requests that when the Service Desk agent clicks on the information icon for the Caller's name, the quick view frame shows only the following fields:

User name -

Manager name -

Email Address -

Employee ID -
How would you modify the quick view frame?

options.text: Update the sys_popup view for the user table
Update the sys_quick view for the caller table
Update the sys_popup view for the caller table
Update the sys_quick view for the user table

questions.explanation: The quick view popup that appears when clicking the info icon next to a reference field is controlled by the sys_popup view for that table. Since the Caller field references the User [sys_user] table, you modify the sys_popup view on the user table (A) to control which fields display. sys_quick (B, D) is not the correct view name, and the caller table doesn't exist — it's the sys_user table.

questions.stem: Your customer has built a mature knowledge base, with articles targeted to internal audiences -which are technical. Other articles are written for end users, with simple instructions. From the Incident form, the agents would like to be able to identify which articles are visible to the callers What feature would you use, to satisfy this requirement?
questions.explanation: The 'Search as User' feature (B) allows agents to see knowledge search results as they would appear to a specific user, respecting that user's access permissions and user criteria. This lets agents identify which articles are visible to callers before sharing. Internal/External Highlighting (A), Show User Viewable (C), and User Only View (D) are not standard Knowledge Management features for this purpose.

questions.stem: Your customer is using the baseline Create Incident Catalog Item and would like to add a few additional input fields. How should you update the catalog item?
questions.explanation: Catalog Builder (C) is the tool for editing catalog items including the baseline Create Incident item. It provides a guided interface for adding variables, modifying layouts, and configuring fulfillment. Catalog Item Designer (A) and Item Designer (B) are not standard tools. Form Designer (D) modifies platform form layouts, not catalog item variable forms.

questions.stem:
Your customer is complaining that Service Desk users keep accidentally assigning Incidents to the Network CAB, instead of Network Support You have confirmed that:
The Network Support group record has the Group types: Incident and Change
The Network CAB group record has the Group type: Change
What could you do on the incident form, for the Assignment Group field, to resolve this issue?

options.text: Add a UI action to hide the Network CAB group from the list
Add a UI action to provide an error message if the Network CAB group is selected
Add Dictionary Override to specify the Incident group Reference Qualifier
Modify the choice list to include only the appropriate group types

questions.explanation: Adding a Dictionary Override to specify a Reference Qualifier on the Assignment Group field (C) is the correct approach. A reference qualifier filters the list to show only groups matching specific criteria (e.g., type=incident). This applies globally on the Incident form. UI actions (A, B) are point solutions, not field filtering. Choice list modification (D) doesn't apply to reference fields.

questions.stem: Which Agent workspace feature gives agents automatic search results that show possible solutions for records they open?
questions.explanation: Agent Assist (E) automatically searches and displays possible solutions when agents open records in the Agent Workspace. It proactively shows knowledge articles, similar incidents, and other relevant content. Chat Bot (A) handles conversations. Related Search Results (B) requires manual configuration. Knowledge Bases (C) store articles but don't auto-search. Intelligent Agent (D) is not a standard feature name.

questions.stem: Which capability provides visibility to data joined between multiple tables?
questions.explanation: Database Views (A) provide visibility into data joined between multiple tables by creating a virtual table that combines columns from different source tables into a single queryable view. Metric Tables (B) store time-series data. Published Reports (C) display data but don't join tables at the data model level. Custom Tables (D) are standalone. Breakdown Sources (E) are PA components.

questions.stem: What tools are available to the assignee to help resolve an Incident? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Incident assignees can use Knowledge Articles (A) to find documented solutions and Workarounds (B) from related Problem records to help resolve incidents. CI Class Manager (C) is for CMDB administration. Incident Overview Dashboard (D) is for managers. Enterprise CMDB Dashboard (E) is for CMDB health monitoring — none of these are resolution tools for assignees.

questions.stem: When using Inbound Email Actions, what happens if an email is received which has no watermark or reference number?

options.text: New incident created from the message
New interaction is created from the message
Email is rejected and auto-reply sent to sender
New case is created from the message

questions.explanation: When an inbound email has no watermark or reference number to match an existing record, the default Inbound Email Action creates a new incident from the message (A). Watermarks and reference numbers are used to match emails to existing records. Without them, the system treats the email as a new request. It doesn't create interactions (B), reject the email (C), or create cases (D) by default.

questions.stem: Under what circumstances, should you use the Communicate workaround Related Link on the Problem record?

options.text: The workaround is helpful information for the Callers on the Problem's related Incidents (open)
The workaround should be published to a knowledge article, visible from the portal
The workaround is helpful information for the members of the Problem's Assignment Group
The workaround is helpful information for the members of the Problem's Work notes list

questions.explanation: The Communicate workaround related link on a Problem record posts the workaround information to the work notes of all OPEN incidents related to that problem. This is helpful for callers on the Problem's related incidents (A) because agents working those incidents can then use the workaround to help resolve them. It doesn't publish to KB (B) or target Assignment Group (C) or Work notes list (D) specifically.

questions.stem: Which interface is designed for tier 1 IT agents who solve internal or external customer issues?
questions.explanation: The IT Service Management Workspace (Agent Workspace) (B) is purpose-built for tier 1 IT agents handling internal or external customer issues. It provides a unified interface with multi-tab navigation, Agent Assist, and optimized layouts. ITSM Dashboard (A) is for reporting. ITIL Homepage (C) is the classic UI landing page. Incident Overview (D) provides management metrics.

questions.stem: When using Agent assist in the Agent workspace, what are examples of possible solutions can be automatically searched and displayed? (Choose five.)
questions.explanation: Agent Assist in Agent Workspace automatically searches and displays: Knowledge articles (B), Problems (D), Changes (E), Cases (F), and Incidents (G). These five record types are surfaced as potential solutions. Runbook Actions (A) are not searched by Agent Assist. SQL Queries (C) are not a ServiceNow feature accessible through Agent Assist.

questions.stem: Which module is a useful starting point for a manager to view current state operational information for Incident management?
questions.explanation: The Incident > Overview module (B) is the best starting point for managers to view current operational information. It displays key metrics like open incidents by priority, assignment group performance, SLA compliance, and trending data. CMDB Health Dashboard (A) is for CMDB. Manager Workspace (C) is not the specific module. Critical Incidents Map (D) is not a standard module name.

questions.stem: The Problem table is extended from what table?
questions.explanation: The Problem table extends from the Task table (A). In ServiceNow, Task is the parent table for most work-tracking records, including Incident, Problem, Change Request, and others. Major Incident (B), Outage (C), Problem Task (D), and Incident (E) are all separate table extensions — Problem directly extends Task, not any of these.

questions.stem:
The Problem Manager wants the Problem Coordinators to be able to Re-analyze a Completed Problem.
Which module could they use to make this change?
questions.explanation: The Problem > Administration > Problem Properties module (A) controls Problem lifecycle settings, including the ability for Problem Coordinators to re-analyze completed problems. This module contains properties governing problem behavior including state transitions. UI Action Groups (B), State Models (C), Form Actions (D), and UI Actions (E) could work but aren't the recommended approach for this configuration.

questions.stem:
Your Problem Manager has a structured problem management process, which includes a final review of the solution implemented and of the data regarding incident reduction. When a problem is resolved, after implementing a fix, they want the Post Fix Review task to be automatically created and assigned to the Problem assignee.
What feature would you use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Flow Designer (E) is the tool for automating the creation of Post Fix Review tasks when a problem is resolved. You can configure a flow triggered by the Problem state changing to Resolved that automatically creates a task assigned to the Problem assignee. State Model (A) manages states. Workflow Dashboard (B) monitors workflows. Action Modeler (C) is not standard. Task Creator (D) is not a platform feature.

questions.stem: Your customer needs help defining Category values for the Problem records. What approach should you suggest? (Choose two.)

options.text: Re-use existing categories from legacy systems
Define categories based on the customer’s CMDB classes
Re-use existing categories from incident management
Define categories based on ITIL problem taxonomy

questions.explanation: Best practice for defining Problem categories is to base them on CMDB classes (B) since problems relate to CIs and their categories, and to reuse existing Incident management categories (C) for consistency across the ITSM processes. Reusing legacy system categories (A) risks importing irrelevant taxonomy. ITIL doesn't define a specific problem taxonomy (D) — categories should reflect the organization's actual service model.

questions.stem: When a user clicks on the Communicate fix UI action on the Problem form, what happens?

options.text: Fix is written to the Comments field on any Incident associated with the problem, which is On Hold, Awaiting Problem
Fix is written to the Work notes field on any Incident associated with the problem, which is Active
Fix is written to the Comments field on any Incident associated with the problem, which is Active
Fix is written to a draft Knowledge article

questions.explanation: When clicking Communicate Fix on the Problem form, the fix information is written to the Work notes field on any ACTIVE incident associated with the problem (B). Work notes are used because the fix is operational information for agents, not customer-facing content. It doesn't go to Comments (A, C) which are customer-visible, and it doesn't create a KB article (D). Only active incidents receive the communication.

questions.stem: Users with which role can Communicate a workaround or fix? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Users with the problem_coordinator (B) and problem_admin (D) roles can Communicate a workaround or fix. The problem_coordinator role manages the problem lifecycle including communicating resolutions. problem_admin has all problem management capabilities. itil_admin (A) is a broader role without specific problem communication rights. problem_task_analyst (C) works on individual tasks, not the overall problem communication.

questions.stem: When a user clicks on the Communicate workaround UI action on the Problem form, what happens?

options.text: Workaround is written to the Comments field on any open Incident associated with the problem
Workaround is written to the Workaround field on any incident associated with the problem
Workaround is written to a draft Knowledge article
Workaround is written to the Work notes field on any open Incident associated with the problem

questions.explanation: When clicking Communicate workaround on the Problem form, the workaround is written to the Work notes field on any open incident associated with the problem (D). Work notes target the technical staff working the incident. It's not written to Comments (A) which are customer-visible, not to a Workaround field on incidents (B), and not to a KB article (C). The communication goes specifically to open incidents.

questions.stem:
A tester wants to submit a bug report, because they are not able to see the Communicate Fix link under the Related Links on the Problem form.
What do you recommend that they confirm, before submitting the bug report? (Choose two.)

options.text: Tester is impersonating a user with communications.manager role
Tester is impersonating the assignee, which has the problem_coordinator role
Tester is impersonating a user with problem_coordinator role
The Fix notes field is filled in and saved

questions.explanation: To see the Communicate Fix link, two conditions must be met: the user must have the problem_coordinator role (C) — not just be the assignee — and the Fix notes field must be filled in and saved (D). The link only appears when there's fix content to communicate. communications.manager (A) is not the required role. Being the assignee alone (B) is insufficient without the proper role.

questions.stem: Problem and Problem Task records, move automatically from New to Assess states, when which fields are filled? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Problem and Problem Task records automatically move from New to Assess when the State field is set appropriately (B) and the Assigned to field is populated (C). The system requires an assignee before the record can progress to assessment. Short Descriptor (A) is not a standard field name (it's Short description). Configuration Item (D) is not required for this automatic state transition.

questions.stem: On a Change Approval Definition record, what does the ‘wait for’ condition define?

options.text: Whether the change approval is sent to an individual user or a group
The state the change must be in before the approval notifications can be sent
The number or percentage of users from the approval group that must approve the change
The fields that must be populated before the approval can be requested

questions.explanation: The 'wait for' condition on a Change Approval Definition defines the number or percentage of users from the approval group that must approve (C). For example, 'wait for: Anyone' means one approval is sufficient, while 'wait for: Everyone' requires all members to approve. It doesn't define individual vs group (A), required state (B), or mandatory fields (D).

questions.stem: In what table are Change records stored?
questions.explanation: Change records are stored in the Change Request [change_request] table (C). The table name is change_request and the display name is Change Request. change_task (A) stores change tasks. rfc (B), change (D), and task_change (E) are not valid ServiceNow table names for change records.

questions.stem:
Risk is configured by default, to calculate Risk = High for a change that is scheduled with only 3 days lead time. Your customer’s change policy requires that changes be requested with 5 days lead time.
How would you satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Update the Risk Property for Insufficient lead time
Update the Risk Assessment Matrix for Insufficient lead time
Update the Calculate Risk UI Action
Update the Risk Matrix for insufficient lead time
Update the Risk Condition for Insufficient lead time

questions.explanation: To change the lead time threshold for risk calculation, you update the Risk Condition for Insufficient lead time (E). Risk Conditions define the criteria used by the risk calculator. The 'Insufficient lead time' condition evaluates the scheduled date versus the current date. You'd modify the condition from 3 days to 5 days. Risk Property (A), Risk Assessment Matrix (B), Calculate Risk UI Action (C), and Risk Matrix (D) are not the correct configuration points.

questions.stem: How are Releases related to Projects?

options.text: Project tasks and Release tasks are interchangeable
Projects can be part of one or more releases
Project features are components of a release
Projects need to be completed before releases can be defined
Projects are used to do root cause analysis for releases

questions.explanation: Projects can be part of one or more releases (B). In ServiceNow, Release Management groups related changes and projects into a release. A project represents the execution work, and it can participate in multiple release cycles. Tasks aren't interchangeable (A). Features are products of releases, not projects (C). Projects don't need to complete first (D). Projects don't do RCA for releases (E).

questions.stem: What baseline Change Flows support the baseline Normal Change model?

options.text: Change - Normal - Assess, Change - Normal - Authorize, Change - Normal - Implement Change - Implementation tasks
Change - Normal - New, Change - Normal - Review, Change - Normal - Close, Change - Implementation tasks
Change - Normal - New, Change - Normal - Assess, Change - Normal - Implement, Change - Implementation tasks
Change - Normal - Assess, Change - Normal - Authorize, Change - Normal - Close, Change - Implementation tasks

questions.explanation: The baseline Normal Change model uses these flows: Change - Normal - Assess (handles assessment and technical approvals), Change - Normal - Authorize (handles CAB/authorization), Change - Normal - Implement (handles implementation), and Change - Implementation tasks (creates implementation tasks). Option A correctly lists all four flows in the Normal model's flow set.

questions.stem: Which of the following Change Task Types are available by default? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The default Change Task Types are Planning (A), Testing (B), and Review (C). These are the baseline task types available on change tasks for organizing implementation activities. Deployment (D) and Verification (E) are not default change task types in the out-of-box configuration. Additional types can be added via the Choice list for the change_task Type field.

questions.stem: What is the Business Rule that triggers automatic group assignment on Incident, Problem or Change requests?

options.text: Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO

questions.explanation: The business rule 'Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO' (A) automatically sets the Assignment group on Incident, Problem, and Change records. It checks the CI's Support group first; if empty, it falls back to the Service Offering's Support group. The other options (B, C, D) are not the actual baseline business rule name in ServiceNow.

questions.stem: In the CAB workbench, what are some ways the CAB manager can identify the Change requests to be added to a particular meeting agenda? (Choose two.)

options.text: Change requests meeting different conditions, like Risk level or Type
Change requests planned within a certain date range
Use any of the options on the Agenda Criteria Tab
Change requests for a certain Change Flow Definition

questions.explanation: In the CAB workbench, managers can identify changes for the agenda by: change requests meeting different conditions like Risk level or Type (A), and change requests planned within a certain date range (B). These filtering options help build focused meeting agendas. 'Agenda Criteria Tab' (C) is not a specific tab name. Change Flow Definition (D) is not used for agenda filtering.

questions.stem: A change user complains that with the new Preapproved tab, they have to search through many options to find the Reboot Windows Server change. Since they use this change several times per day, it is inconvenient. What should you suggest to make it easier for the change user?

options.text: Drag the change tile to the Navigation pane

questions.explanation: The Pin feature (A) allows change users to pin a frequently used standard change template to the top of the Preapproved tab for quick access. This eliminates searching through many options. Favorites (B) are not a standard feature on the change landing page. Keyword search (C) still requires typing each time. Dragging to Navigation pane (D) is not supported functionality.

questions.stem: Roles control which users can perform which actions on a change record. What are actions, which cannot be performed by anyone, even an administrator? (Choose two.)

options.text: Update Change Type on an existing change record

questions.explanation: Two actions that cannot be performed by anyone, including administrators: updating the Change Type on an existing change record (A) — once created, the type is locked, and deleting a Standard Change Template (C) — templates can only be retired, not deleted. Deleting a Change record (B) is possible for admins. Deleting a CAB Definition (D) is also possible for users with appropriate roles.

questions.stem: In the baseline Change - Normal model how can Change Tasks be added? (Choose two.)

options.text: Automatically via the Change - Implementation subflow
Manually by the user during New, Assess, and Authorized states
Automatically depending on the category selected on the Change Request
Manually by the user during all states, except Closed or Canceled

questions.explanation: In the baseline Normal Change model, change tasks can be added: automatically via the Change - Implementation subflow (A) which creates implementation tasks, and manually by the user during all states except Closed or Canceled (D). Manual task creation isn't limited to New/Assess/Authorized (B). Tasks aren't auto-created based on category (C) — the Implementation subflow handles automatic creation.

questions.stem: In the baseline Change - Normal model, when the Change request goes to the Review state, what happens to the implementation and testing tasks, if they have not been closed.

options.text: They are automatically assigned to the Change assignee and closed
An error displays, requiring that the Tasks be closed before moving to Review

questions.explanation: When a Normal Change moves to Review state, any open implementation and testing tasks that haven't been closed are automatically canceled (A). This prevents orphaned tasks from lingering after the review phase begins. They aren't automatically closed (B) or reassigned and closed (C). No error is displayed blocking the transition (D) — the system handles this automatically.

questions.stem: On the Unauthorized Change Properties module what can you configure? (Choose two.)

options.text: Maximum number of unauthorized change records for a CI

questions.explanation: The Unauthorized Change Properties module lets you configure: Enable/Disable creation of unauthorized changes (A) to turn the feature on or off, and CI classes to monitor (D) to specify which CI types trigger unauthorized change detection. Maximum number of records (B) and Dashboard configuration (C) are not settings available in this module.

questions.stem: How do you describe the relationship between a Knowledge article and a Knowledge base category?

options.text: Articles can only be published to one category
Articles must be published to at least one category
Articles must be approved by the selected category owner
Articles can be published to a category and subcategory

questions.explanation: Knowledge articles can only be published to one category (A). Each article has a single Category field that determines its placement in the knowledge base hierarchy. Articles cannot span multiple categories. They don't require publication to at least one (B) — unpublished articles have no category requirement. Category owner approval (C) is not required. Items can't simultaneously be in a category and subcategory (D) separately.

questions.stem: What are the different ways a user can provide feedback on a knowledge article? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Users can provide feedback on knowledge articles via: Comment on Article (B) for written feedback, Helpful? (C) for yes/no usefulness rating, Flag Article (D) to report issues, and 5-star scale (E) for rating quality. 10-star scale (A) is not a standard feedback mechanism. Pin Article (F) is not a user feedback feature — it's a personal organization tool.

questions.stem: When using the Knowledge - instant Retire workflow, how does the Valid to date enact a Knowledge article?

options.text: On Valid to date, article is automatically retired
On Valid to date, retire notification is sent to the Knowledge article author
On Valid to date, retire notification is sent to the Knowledge base owner
On Valid to date, the article is archived

questions.explanation: When using the Knowledge - Instant Retire workflow, the article is automatically retired on the Valid to date (A). This workflow immediately moves the article to retired state when the date arrives, without requiring approval. It doesn't send notifications to the author (B) or KB owner (C), and it doesn't archive (D) — it retires. The 'Instant' in the name reflects the automatic, no-approval retirement.

questions.stem:
In the ServiceNow native platform, the service catalog can be accessed via the Self-Service > Service Catalog module. Your customer wants to make modifications to this home page, to add, remove and re-arrange the categories.
Users with what roles can make these edits? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Users with the catalog_admin (A) and admin (E) roles can modify the Service Catalog home page to add, remove, and rearrange categories. catalog_admin is the primary role for catalog management. The admin role has full system access. sc_catalog_admin (B), catalog_editor (C), and sn_catalog_homepage_write (D) are not standard roles for this specific homepage editing capability.

questions.stem: What would you use to create a New Hire Employee request which would allow you to order your workstation and company mobile?
questions.explanation: An Order Guide (D) allows you to bundle multiple catalog items into a single request — perfect for a New Hire who needs a workstation AND a company mobile. The Order Guide presents a guided experience to order multiple items together. A Knowledge item (A) provides information only. Record Producer (B) creates non-catalog records. A single Catalog Item (C) handles one item. Content Item (E) is informational.

questions.stem: Which tool allows process owners to use natural language to automate approvals, tasks, notifications and other record operations with little to no code?
questions.explanation: Flow Designer (C) enables process owners to use natural language descriptions and low/no-code tools to automate approvals, tasks, notifications, and record operations. It provides a visual interface for building automation. Workflow Mapper (A), Workflow Manager (B), Flow Dashboard (D), and Process Designer (E) are not the correct tool names for this low-code automation capability.

questions.stem: What process is responsible for defining and managing the lifecycle of all catalog items, by producing and maintaining the services in the catalog and ensuring that a central, accurate, and consistent source of data is provided?
questions.explanation: Service Catalog Management (D) is the ITIL process responsible for defining and managing the lifecycle of all catalog items, maintaining services in the catalog, and ensuring a central, consistent data source. Service Portfolio Management (A) manages the broader service portfolio. Catalog Item Management (B) is not a defined ITIL process. Service Mapping (C) discovers application infrastructure.

questions.stem:
Your customer needs different catalogs for:
Human Resources - employee facing - for submitting requests to HR
Customer - external customer facing - for ordering company products and services
When these catalogs are created, in which table would the definition be stored?
questions.explanation: Catalog definitions are stored in the Catalog [sc_catalog] table (B). When creating multiple catalogs for different purposes (HR, Customer-facing), each catalog record exists in sc_catalog with its configuration, categories, and access settings. bs_catalog (A), sc_portfolio (C), and sn_offering (D) are not the correct table names for catalog definitions.

questions.stem: When creating a catalog, which field specifies who can edit, update, and delete catalogs, categories, and catalog items?
questions.explanation: The Manager field (A) on a catalog record specifies who can edit, update, and delete catalogs, categories, and catalog items. The Manager has full administrative control over the catalog's structure and content. Contributors (B) is not a standard catalog field. Owner (C) is not used for edit permissions on the catalog record. Editors (D) have creation capabilities but Manager controls the overall governance.

questions.stem: Which type of catalog item may be found in a Service Catalog?
questions.explanation: Record Producers (B) are a type of catalog item found in the Service Catalog. They create records in target tables other than the standard sc_req_item table. Requested Items (A) are the OUTPUT of ordering catalog items, not items themselves. Categories (C) organize items but aren't items. Execution Plans (D) define fulfillment steps but aren't catalog items.

questions.stem: Which of the following are users able to do when configuring stages in Flow Designer? (Choose two.)

options.text: Display the stages to the requester
Import a copy of a pre-defined stage set
Define the stage set in a subflow

questions.explanation: When configuring stages in Flow Designer, users can: create any number of stages (B) to define the fulfillment process steps, and import a copy of a pre-defined stage set (C) to reuse common stage configurations. Displaying stages to requesters (A) happens automatically via the request process. Defining the stage set in a subflow (D) is not how stages are configured — they're defined at the flow level.

questions.stem: When creating a catalog, which field specifies who is able to create, modify, and publish items in the catalog?
questions.explanation: The Editors field (A) on a catalog record specifies who can create, modify, and publish items in the catalog. Editors have the ability to manage catalog item content within the catalog. Item Admins (B), Item Owners (C), and Authors (D) are not standard field names on the catalog record for this editing capability.

questions.stem: When defining catalog categories and subcategories, what are some good practices to follow? (Choose two.)

options.text: Align categories with CMDB classes where possible
Keep the number of top-level categories to 8-10
Remember that items can only be assigned to one category
Do not go to deep with subcategories: go only 1-2 levels deep

questions.explanation: Good practices for catalog categories: keep the number of top-level categories to 8-10 (B) to avoid overwhelming users, and don't go deeper than 1-2 levels with subcategories (D) as deep nesting makes navigation difficult. Aligning with CMDB classes (A) is a Problem category practice, not catalog. Items CAN be assigned to multiple categories via the sc_cat_item_category m2m table (C is incorrect).

questions.stem:
In request fulfillment, approvals can be required before a request can be fulfilled. Your customer is worried about requests getting stuck in the process flow, if the approver is on extended absence from the office.
What can you suggest to alleviate this concern? (Choose two.)

options.text: The approver can use the Delegate module to assign a person to approve on their behalf, while they are away from the office
The approver can set their approval notifications to forward to their personal email address
The approval can be defined as a group approval, where any member of the group can approve
The approver can set their approval notifications to auto-reply with “approved” in the subject line

questions.explanation: To handle absent approvers: the Delegate module (A) lets approvers assign a delegate who can approve on their behalf during their absence, and defining a group approval (C) means any member of the approval group can approve, so one person's absence doesn't block the process. Forwarding to personal email (B) doesn't enable approval capability. Auto-reply (D) is not a supported approval mechanism.

questions.stem: Released in Quebec, what tool enables you to delegate the creation and maintenance of common and simple use case Catalog Items to business users?
questions.explanation: Catalog Builder (D) was released in Quebec to enable business users to create and maintain common catalog items with little to no coding. It provides a guided, step-by-step interface for building items, variables, and basic fulfillment. Catalog Wizard (A), Catalog Designer (B), and Catalog Item Builder (C) are not the official names for this Quebec-release feature.

questions.stem: Request fulfillment relies on three record types, Requests, Requested Items, and Catalog Tasks. The lifecycle status of these records is reflected in a combination of state and stage fields. Which status field is set by the flow?
questions.explanation: The Stage field on Requested Items (A) is set by the flow. Flows control the progression through stages (e.g., Waiting for Approval → Fulfillment → Complete), and each flow action can advance the stage. The State fields on Request, Requested Item, and Catalog Task records are managed separately — but Stage specifically is flow-driven to reflect the overall fulfillment progress.

questions.stem:
Your implementation team has a new Business Analyst. They will be attending their first Service Catalog workshop and will be responsible for capturing notes and decisions from the workshop.
What Now Create assets do you recommend they review, to prepare? (Choose two.)

options.text: Service Catalog and Request Mgmt - Workshop Preparation Guide
Service Catalog and Request Mgmt - Process Guide
IT Service Management - Typical Challenges and Remediation
ITSM - Business Outcomes and Corresponding KPIs

questions.explanation: For a new Business Analyst preparing for a Service Catalog workshop: the Workshop Preparation Guide (A) provides pre-workshop information and templates, and the Process Guide (B) explains the Service Catalog and Request Management processes in detail. Typical Challenges (C) and Business Outcomes/KPIs (D) are broader ITSM resources not specifically focused on catalog workshop preparation.

questions.stem: Which role would give you access to the CI Class Manager?
questions.explanation: The ecmdb_admin role (A) provides access to the CI Class Manager for managing CMDB class hierarchy. The 'e' prefix stands for Enterprise CMDB. ecmdb (B) is not the admin-level role. class_manager (C) and sn_class_manager (D) are not standard ServiceNow roles for CI Class Manager access.

questions.stem: What module do you use to change the setting for the time between incident Resolution and Closure?
questions.explanation: The Incident Properties module (D) is where you configure the time between incident Resolution and Closure. This module contains the auto-closure property that defines how many days after resolution an incident automatically closes. ITSM Properties (A) covers broader ITSM settings. System Settings (B) is too general. Incident Settings (C) and Resolution Properties (E) are not the correct module names.

questions.stem: By default, when using Inbound actions, what happens if an email is received which has an Incident watermark?

options.text: Incident record is updated, per the action's script
Auto-reply sent to sender, recommending they use Portal chat
Incident record is re-set to state = attention required

questions.explanation: When an inbound email contains an Incident watermark, the default behavior is to update the existing incident record per the Inbound Email Action's script (B). The watermark identifies which incident to update. The SLA clock isn't automatically unpaused (A). No auto-reply is sent (C). The state isn't set to 'attention required' (D). The action's script determines exactly what fields get updated.

questions.stem: When using the Email Client, what is the difference between an Email Template and a Quick Message?

options.text: Email Templates are like forms that can be sent to the caller for completion; Quick Messages are primarily used by the Chat Bot
Email Template is defined and automatically applied when the email form launches; Quick Messages are defined and then can be manually applied by the user
Email Templates are included with ITSM; Quick Messages are new with Machine Learning
Email templates are defined by users with admin role; Quick Messages are defined by users with quick_message_admin role

questions.explanation: An Email Template is defined and automatically applied when the email form launches (pre-populating subject, body, recipients), while Quick Messages are defined templates that can be manually selected and applied by the user at any time (B). They aren't forms (A). Quick Messages aren't ML-based (C). Both can be defined by various roles, not just admin/quick_message_admin (D).

questions.stem: Your customer wants incidents to close automatically 7 days after the incident is resolved. How do you meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

options.text: Modify the Incident Lifecycle flow to trigger from the Resolved date instead of the Updated date
Update the incident_close UI action script
From the Incident Properties application, set Enable auto closure of incidents based on Resolution date to Yes
Modify the Incident Lifecycle flow to expire after 7 days

questions.explanation: To auto-close incidents 7 days after resolution: modify the Incident Lifecycle flow to trigger from the Resolved date instead of Updated date (A), and from Incident Properties, enable auto-closure based on Resolution date (C). Both settings work together to trigger closure based on when the incident was resolved. Editing the UI action script (B) is not the proper approach. Setting flow expiry (D) doesn't target the resolution-to-close interval.

questions.stem: What tools are available to the assignee to help resolve an Incident? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Incident assignees use Known Errors (A) to find documented root causes and workarounds, and Resolutions from similar incidents (B) to apply proven solutions. These are the primary resolution tools available to assignees. CI Class Manager (C) is for CMDB administration. Incident Overview Dashboard (D) is for managers. Enterprise CMDB Dashboard (E) monitors CMDB health.

questions.stem: Your customer wants to use the Service Catalog to generate task-based records for end-user inquiries. What Service Catalog capability can you use to generate these records?
questions.explanation: Record Producers (D) generate task-based records (like incidents, problems, etc.) from the Service Catalog. You configure a Record Producer with a target table to create records of that type when submitted. Execution Plans (A) define fulfillment steps. Content Items (B) are informational links. Catalog Items (C) create Requested Items, not arbitrary task records.

questions.stem: Which type of catalog item may be found in a Service Catalog?
questions.explanation: Order Guides (B) are a type of catalog item found in the Service Catalog. They bundle multiple items into a single guided ordering experience. Requested Items (A) are the output of ordering, not items themselves. Categories (C) organize items but aren't items. Execution Plans (D) define fulfillment workflows, not catalog item types.

questions.stem: From which table, is the Incident table extended?
questions.explanation: The Incident table extends from Task [task] (A). Task is the foundational parent table for work-tracking records in ServiceNow, including Incident, Problem, Change Request, and more. Task [sn_task] (B) is not the correct table name. Ticket [ticket] (C) and Work [sn_work] (D) don't exist as standard ServiceNow tables.

questions.stem: What optional Incident table is extended from the Task table?
questions.explanation: The Incident Task [incident_task] table (C) extends from the Task table and is an optional table for breaking incident work into sub-tasks. Child Incident (A), Major Incident (B) as a separate table, and Parent Incident (D) are not optional Incident tables extending Task. The Incident Task table must be enabled via Incident Properties.

questions.stem: Category and Subcategory values can be set manually on the Incident form. What are disadvantages of this approach? (Choose two.)

options.text: Too many options may confuse users and increase mis-categorization
Choices have no additional metadata to drive process
It is not part of the baseline instance

questions.explanation: Disadvantages of manually setting Category/Subcategory values: too many options may confuse users and increase mis-categorization (A), and choices have no additional metadata to drive process automation (B) — unlike service-based categorization tied to CMDB. It's not particularly difficult to implement (C), and manual category/subcategory IS part of the baseline instance (D).

questions.stem: When using the baseline business rule, Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO, what behavior would you expect on an Incident form? (Choose two.)

options.text: If selected CI does not have an Owner group, write the Support group from the Service Offering to the Assignment group field
If selected CI has a Support group, write that group to the Assignment group field
If selected CI has an Owner group, write that group to the Assignment group field
If selected CI does not have a Support group, write the Support group from the Service Offering to the Assignment group field

questions.explanation: The 'Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO' business rule: if the selected CI has a Support group, writes that group to the Assignment group field (B), and if the CI doesn't have a Support group, writes the Support group from the Service Offering (D). It checks CI Support group first, then falls back to Service Offering. Owner group (A, C) is not part of this business rule's logic.

questions.stem: On an incident record, where are the fields that appear on the caller lookup select box defined?

options.text: The Caller lookup field on the [user] table
The ref_ac_column attribute from the dictionary entry
The ref_contributions attribute on the caller lookup form
The form design of the caller lookup form

questions.explanation: The fields appearing in the caller lookup select box (typeahead/autocomplete dropdown) are defined by the ref_ac_columns attribute in the dictionary entry (B) for that reference field. This attribute specifies which columns from the referenced table appear in the autocomplete results. It's not defined on the user table directly (A), ref_contributions (C), or form design (D).

questions.stem: Where do you enable the Search as feature for an incident?
questions.explanation: The 'Search as' feature is enabled for an incident through the Related Search Results table configuration (C). This feature allows agents to search knowledge as if they were a different user. It's configured in the agent_intelligence_config or related search results configuration, not via system properties (A), Incident Properties (B), or form design (D).

questions.stem: If the Assignment group is empty on an incident record, what happens when an agent that is a member of a single user groups clicks the Assign to me UI action?

options.text: The agent is prompted to select the Assignment group
The Assignment group field is populated with agent’s user group
An error is displayed indicating the Assignment group field must be populated before executing the Assign to me UI action
The Assignment group field remains empty

questions.explanation: When an agent who is a member of a single user group clicks 'Assign to me', the Assignment group field is populated with the agent's user group (B) and the Assigned to field is set to the agent. Since they belong to only one group, the system automatically selects it. No prompt (A) or error (C) is needed. The field doesn't remain empty (D) because the system can determine the group unambiguously.

questions.stem: A problem record is the Parent to what record?
questions.explanation: A Problem record is the parent to Problem Task records (D). Problem Tasks are child records used to break the investigation into manageable work items like root cause analysis, testing, and fix implementation. Known Error (A) is a knowledge article type. Workaround (B) is a field value. Major Incident (C) relates to incidents. Related Incidents (E) are associated records, not child records.

questions.stem:
When you create a problem from an incident, impact, urgency and priority are automatically populated, from the incident record. Your problem management process owner wants the problem manager to be responsible for assessing the impact and urgency on the problem, so they don't want the values from incident to be copied over.
What module would you use to make this adjustment?

options.text: System Policy > Rules > Priority Lookup Rules

questions.explanation: Problem > Administration > Problem Properties (B) is the module for configuring whether impact and urgency are copied from incidents to new problems. This module contains properties controlling problem creation behavior, including whether to inherit incident field values. Priority Lookup Rules (A) manage priority calculation. ITSM Properties (C) is broader. Incident Properties (D) manages incident settings, not problem settings.

questions.stem: As of Quebec, Problem task records will move automatically from one state, to another state, provided the required fields are filled. What are those states?

options.text: On Hold to Work in Progress

questions.explanation: As of Quebec, Problem Task records automatically move from New to Assess (C) when required fields (Assigned to) are populated. This automatic state transition ensures tasks progress through the lifecycle. Assess to Work in Progress (A) requires manual action. On Hold to WIP (B) is not an automatic transition. Draft to Assess (D) — there is no Draft state for problem tasks. WIP to Closed (E) is not automatic.

questions.stem: A new problem manager wants to know how to create reports for monitoring problem management activities. What do you recommend they do before creating new reports?

options.text: Submit a New Report Request via the service catalog
Take the Performance Analytics fundamentals course
Go to Reports > View/Run > All, then search for Problem reports
Submit a request for the sn_report_creator role

questions.explanation: Before creating new reports, the problem manager should go to Reports > View/Run > All and search for existing Problem reports (C). ServiceNow includes many baseline problem management reports. Creating new reports before reviewing existing ones wastes effort. Submitting a catalog request (A), taking a PA course (B), requesting a role (D), and turning on data collection (E) are premature steps.

questions.stem: Your customer wants to know why users with the problem_coordinator role can Communicate workarounds, and fixes; but users with problem_task_analyst cannot. How do you explain this?

options.text: The technical resources working on the problem investigation are focused on the technical details, and may provide information that is not useful for the callers
The problem coordinator is the only role with the ability to recall a message
The problem coordinator is responsible for approving or rejecting the proposed message
The message will be automatically displayed on the Portal

questions.explanation: Problem_task_analysts focus on technical investigation details and may provide information not useful for callers (A). The problem_coordinator role handles communication because they understand the broader context and can frame the workaround/fix appropriately for the incident agents. It's not about message recall (B), approval (C), or portal display (D) — it's about ensuring communications are meaningful and actionable.

questions.stem: A user wants to know what makes the Known Error knowledge base in ServiceNow different from all other knowledge bases. How should you respond?

options.text: The Known Error knowledge base documents problems that are under investigation, but not yet have a root cause
Only users with sn_known_error_write can create Known Error articles
Users with sn_problem_write can create known error articles, but not articles for other knowledge bases
The Known Error knowledge articles use a template, which includes the Workaround and the Cause

questions.explanation: The Known Error knowledge base is unique because its articles use a specific template that includes the Workaround and Cause fields (D). This template structure differentiates Known Error articles from standard KB articles by capturing the root cause and workaround information. It's not about documenting problems under investigation (A), role requirements (B, C) — the template is the distinguishing feature.

questions.stem: Problem management provides what benefits for Incident management? (Choose two.)

options.text: Published workarounds help quickly resolve incidents
Problem investigations automatically triggered for multiple user incidents

questions.explanation: Problem management benefits Incident management by: implementing solutions that reduce future incidents (A), and publishing workarounds that help agents quickly resolve current incidents (B). Problem investigations aren't automatically triggered (C) — they require manual initiation. Incident managers don't authorize problem investigations (D) — that's the problem manager's responsibility.

questions.stem: A tester reports a bug, because they submitted a Known Error article from a Problem record, but it is not visible from the Known Error database. What could cause this?

options.text: The article is in draft state, but has not been published
The Problem Management Best Practice - Madrid - Knowledge Integration plugin has not been activated
The user criteria on the knowledge base is incorrect
The tester is not impersonating an itil user

questions.explanation: The most likely cause is that the article is still in draft state and hasn't been published (A). Knowledge articles must go through the publication workflow before they're visible in the knowledge base. The plugin (B) refers to a best practice plugin but isn't required for basic Known Error functionality. User criteria (C) and itil impersonation (D) are less likely causes than an unpublished article.

questions.stem: Where can a change manager define the conditions that must be met before a change request can move from one state to another?
questions.explanation: Model State Transition Conditions (A) is where change managers define conditions that must be met before a change request can move between states. These conditions specify required fields, approval statuses, and other prerequisites for each state transition. Dictionary Overrides (B) control field behavior. State choices (C) define available states. State conditions (D) is a plausible but incorrect name.

questions.stem: Where can a change manager define the interval frequency for unauthorized change detection?
questions.explanation: The Unauthorized Change Properties module (C) is where you configure the interval frequency for unauthorized change detection scans. This module controls how often the system checks for changes made to CIs outside the change management process. The business rule (A), Event Processing Properties (B), and unauthorized change flow (D) are not where detection interval configuration happens.

questions.stem: Prior to Quebec, when you click Change > Create New, which page is displayed?
questions.explanation: Prior to Quebec, clicking Change > Create New displayed the Change Interceptor (E). The interceptor page presented options for different change types (Normal, Emergency, Standard) and allowed users to select the appropriate template. With Quebec, the Change Landing Page (A) was added for multimodal change. The Change Form (B), Catalog (C), and Wizard (D) are not what displayed by default pre-Quebec.

questions.stem: Inside a change flow, you can automate a task with a sequence of related steps, like looking up a record, creating a record, or applying a policy. What is this component of the flow called?
questions.explanation: Flow Actions (A) are the components within a flow that automate tasks with sequences of related steps like looking up records, creating records, or applying policies. Each action performs a specific operation. Flow Activities (B) is the older Workflow Editor term. Flow Steps (C), Action Pills (D), and Flow Tasks (E) are not the correct terminology for these flow components.

questions.stem: On the Release record, what are the available options on the Release phase list?

options.text: Requirement Gathering, Design, Build, Roll-out, Unit Testing, User Acceptance, Pilot
Scoping, Design, Develop, Deployment, Unit Testing, Integration, Pilot
Analyze, Design, Development, Build, Roll-out, QA, User Acceptance
Requirement Gathering, Design, Development, Build, Deployment, QA, User Acceptance

questions.explanation: The baseline Release phase list options are: Requirement Gathering, Design, Development, Build, Deployment, QA, User Acceptance (D). These phases map to a standard SDLC approach. Option A uses 'Roll-out' and 'Unit Testing/Pilot' which aren't all baseline. Option B uses 'Scoping' and 'Integration'. Option C uses 'Analyze' and 'Roll-out'. The phases track the release from requirements through user acceptance.

questions.stem: You have created a new Change model and added a new Approval Policy for that model. But the newly defined approval is not triggering. What could cause this issue?

options.text: The business rule "Apply approval policy" on the change_request table has not been updated to include the new Approval Policy.
The "Apply Change Approval Policy" action in the flow created for the new change model does not reference the new Approval Policy.
The workflow that triggers the Approval Policy for the new model has not been created using the workflow editor.
The system property "glide.ui.approval.policies" has not been updated to include the new Approval Policy.

questions.explanation: The newly defined approval isn't triggering because the 'Apply Change Approval Policy' action in the flow for the new change model doesn't reference the new Approval Policy (B). Each change model's flow must explicitly include the correct approval policy via the flow action. Business rules (A), workflow editor (C), and system properties (D) are not how approval policies are linked to change models in the Quebec+ approach.

questions.stem: In the Quebec release of Change management, what new architectural features were added?

options.text: Change Flows, Change Designer and Change Approval Matrix
Change Models, Change Flows and State Transition Models
Change PIR Assessments, Change Designer and Change Approval Policies

questions.explanation: The Quebec release introduced Change Models (defining change configurations), Change Flows (automating change lifecycle via Flow Designer), and State Transition Models (controlling state movement with conditions) (C). These three features represent the architectural modernization of Change Management. Catalog Builder (A) is for service catalog. Change Designer (A, B, D) is not a Quebec feature. Approval Matrix (B) and PIR Assessments (D) aren't the key Quebec additions.

questions.stem: In the baseline implementation, what are key relationships between Change and Configuration Item (CI) records? (Choose three.)

options.text: The CI Manager is part of the change approval workflow
One Change can be submitted for multiple CIs
Changes should reference at least one CI
The CI Support Group is responsible for change implementations
A CI can be affected by a change, even if it is not the CI being changed

questions.explanation: Key relationships between Change and CI: one Change can be submitted for multiple CIs (B) via the Affected CIs related list, changes should reference at least one CI (C) as best practice to understand impact, and a CI can be affected by a change even if it isn't the primary CI being changed (E) via the Impacted Services/CIs. CI Manager approval (A) isn't default behavior. CI Support Group (D) doesn't own implementation responsibility.

questions.stem: In Change management, what allows customers to define condition based flows for a fit for purpose model?
questions.explanation: State Transition Models (A) allow customers to define condition-based flows for fit-for-purpose change models. Each state can have transition conditions that must be met (required fields, approvals, etc.) before moving to the next state, enabling model-specific governance. State Flows (B), Workflows 2.0 (C), and Conditional Change Models (D) are not the correct feature names for this capability.

questions.stem: By default, a business rule, causes the Assignment group to be automatically set. How is the group identified?

options.text: Change group on CI record, or if empty, the Change group on the Service offering
Support group on CI record, or the default assignment group for the user
Support group on CI record, or if empty, the Support group on the Service
Support group on CI record, or if empty, the Support group on the Service offering

questions.explanation: The business rule identifies the assignment group by checking the Support group on the CI record first; if empty, it falls back to the Support group on the Service Offering (D). This is the 'Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO' business rule behavior. Change group (A) is not used. Service (C) is not the fallback — Service Offering is. Default user group (B) is not part of this logic.

questions.stem:
Your implementation has some legacy change types with workflows, and also some new change models. What option for Change Create New will support your scenario?
A Change Landing Page
questions.explanation: The Change Interceptor (C) supports scenarios with both legacy change types using workflows AND new change models. It presents an interceptor page where users can choose between different change creation paths, supporting both old and new configurations simultaneously. Change Landing Page (A) is for multimodal only. Change Overview (B) is a dashboard. Change Catalog (D) is not the correct term.

questions.stem: Which Change request fields are used in conflict detection? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Change conflict detection uses: Planned end date (B), Planned start date (D), and Configuration item (E). The system checks for overlapping time windows on the same CI. If another change targets the same CI during the same planned timeframe, a conflict is detected. CI Business criticality (A) and Risk (C) are change attributes but not used in the conflict detection algorithm.

questions.stem: What types of Conflicts are detected automatically on the Change request? (Choose three.)

options.text: Another change for the same CI, at the same time

questions.explanation: Automatically detected conflict types: Conflict with Blackout Schedule (B) when a change falls during a blackout window, another change for the same CI at the same time (D) detecting overlapping changes, and Conflict with Maintenance Window (E) when outside the approved maintenance window. Assignee Shift Schedule (A) and Company Holiday (C) are not part of the standard conflict detection.

questions.stem: How are Releases related to Changes?

options.text: Releases are comprised of one or more Changes
Changes are comprised of one or more Releases
Releases are implemented prior to Changes
Changes are implemented prior to Releases

questions.explanation: Releases are comprised of one or more Changes (A). A release bundles related changes together for coordinated deployment. Changes represent individual modifications, while the release manages their collective planning, testing, and deployment. Changes are not comprised of releases (B). Neither is implemented strictly before the other (C, D) — they're coordinated together.

questions.stem: Which workflow is defined as: Requests approval from a manager of the knowledge base before moving the article to the retired state. The workflow is canceled and the article remains in the published state if any manager rejects the request.
questions.explanation: The Knowledge - Approval Retire workflow (C) requests approval from a knowledge base manager before retiring an article. If any manager rejects, the workflow is canceled and the article remains published. Knowledge - Article Retire (A) and Retire Authorize (B) are not standard workflow names. Retire-Approval Required (D) is not the exact name. Instant Retire (E) retires immediately without approval.

questions.stem: What Knowledge base feature can you use to standardize the sections and fonts on a knowledge article?
questions.explanation: Knowledge Templates (C) standardize the sections and formatting of knowledge articles. Templates define the structure (header fields, body sections, required content) ensuring consistent formatting across articles in a knowledge base. Article designer (A) is not a standard feature. Coaching loops (B) are for feedback. Article layout (D) is not the correct term for this standardization feature.

questions.stem: Which of the following roles has the ability to create and manage user criteria for service catalogs?
questions.explanation: The catalog_admin role (A) has the ability to create and manage user criteria for service catalogs. This role provides full administrative control over catalog configuration including access control via user criteria. itil_admin (B) manages ITSM processes. catalog_manager (C), catalog_criteria_admin (D), and catalog_criteria_manager (E) are not standard ServiceNow roles for user criteria management.

questions.stem: Which catalog property allows users to save partially-completed requests to complete and submit at a later time?
questions.explanation: The Enable wish list property (B) allows users to save partially-completed requests to complete and submit later. The wish list acts as a save-for-later feature in the service catalog. Edit cart layout (A) modifies the cart display. Enable cart save (C) and User partial save (D) are not the actual property names — 'wish list' is the ServiceNow term for this save-and-resume capability.

questions.stem: Once a Catalog Item has been requested, what mechanism determines the approvals, and tasks that are triggered in the application?
questions.explanation: Flows (B) determine the approvals and tasks triggered after a catalog item is requested. Flow Designer processes attached to catalog items define the fulfillment logic including approval steps, task creation, and notifications. Processes (A) and Procedures (C) are not ServiceNow terms for this. Actions (D) are components within flows. Scripts (E) are lower-level than the mechanism controlling fulfillment.

questions.stem: Unless there are particular security requirements, what role is given to users that perform request fulfillment work?
questions.explanation: The itil role (A) is the standard role given to users performing request fulfillment work unless there are particular security requirements. It provides access to task-based work across ITSM modules including catalog task fulfillment. task_worker (B) is not the standard ITSM fulfillment role. sc_fulfiller (C), catalog_fulfiller (D), and fulfiller (E) are not standard ServiceNow roles.

questions.stem:
Your customer is a data center. They have a construction department that builds out spaces for new customers. The customer account representatives are responsible for initiating the construction requests. The guidelines are extensive for how to complete the construction request documentation.
Your customer wants the catalog to contain two items:
1. Construction request
2. Getting Started with Construction Requests
The Getting Started Item should contain a link to a Knowledge Article.
What type of item would you use to satisfy the requirement for the Getting Started Item?
questions.explanation: A Content Item (C) is used for informational links, such as linking to a Knowledge Article. Content Items don't create any records or requests — they simply redirect users to content like KB articles, external URLs, or other resources. Knowledge Item (A) is not a standard catalog type. Record Producer (B) creates records. Order Guide (D) bundles items. Catalog Item (E) creates Requested Items.

questions.stem: What is an example of a good use case for an Order Guide?

options.text: Order a case of Laundry Soap

questions.explanation: Ordering a set of Dishes (A) is a good use case for an Order Guide because it involves selecting multiple related items that go together as a set, with guided selection. An Order Guide bundles multiple catalog items with a guided process. A custom automobile (B) is better as a single complex catalog item. A consultation (C), couch (D), and laundry soap (E) are single items not requiring bundling.

questions.stem: Your customer has a catalog item for Request VPN. They would like to adjust the cart layout for only the VPN item, so the Quantity field is not displayed. How would you meet this requirement?

options.text: On the Cart Layout, Columns tab, unselect Quantity column
On the Catalog Item, Columns tab, unselect Quantity column
On the Catalog Item, Advanced View, unselect Use cart layout, select No quantity
On the Catalog, Advanced View, unselect Use cart layout, select No quantity
On the Catalog Item, Cart Layout Related List, set the Quantity record to Inactive

questions.explanation: On the Catalog Item's Advanced View, you can unselect 'Use cart layout' and then select 'No quantity' (C) to hide the Quantity field for only the VPN item. This per-item override lets you customize behavior without affecting other items. Cart Layout (A) would change all items. The Columns tab (B) is not where this setting lives. Catalog-level (D) affects everything. Inactive record (E) isn't the correct approach.

questions.stem: A manager wants to run a report on the Computer catalog items, to see how many requests are being made for the add on extra memory, as compared with those requiring only the base memory. How would you meet this requirement?

options.text: Build report on SC Task table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory
Build report on Requested Item table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory
Build report on Task table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory
Build report on Request table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory
Build report on Catalog Item table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory

questions.explanation: Build a report on the Requested Item table, grouped by Variables for Computer > Extra memory (B). Requested Items track what was ordered from the catalog including variable values. SC Task (A) tracks fulfillment tasks. Task (C) is too broad. Request (D) is the parent container without variable detail. Catalog Item (E) stores the item definition, not request data.

questions.stem: Which record type would you use for an Ask a Question form that would generate an Incident?
questions.explanation: A Record Producer (A) creates records in a specified target table from the Service Catalog. For an 'Ask a Question' form that generates an Incident, you configure a Record Producer targeting the incident table. Order Guide (B) bundles items. Linked Item (C) is not standard. Catalog Item (D) creates Requested Items. Content Item (E) is informational only.

questions.stem: Which of the following objects on the Shopping Cart Widget can be displayed or hidden using Maintain Cart Layouts settings? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Maintain Cart Layouts settings allow showing or hiding Quantity (A) and Price (C) on the Shopping Cart Widget. These are the configurable display elements in the cart layout. Requested by (B) and Shipping Address (D) are not objects controlled through the Cart Layout settings — they are handled through different form configurations.

questions.stem:
Your customer wants a catalog to contain two items:
1. A request with 1 approval and 2 fulfillment tasks
2. A link to a knowledge article
What type of item would you use to satisfy the requirement for the Construction request?
questions.explanation: A Catalog Item (A) is the correct type for a request with 1 approval and 2 fulfillment tasks. Catalog Items handle standard request fulfillment with configurable approval and task flows. Content Item (B) is informational only — that's the Knowledge article link (item 2 in the question). Record Producer (C) creates non-catalog records. Order Guide (D) bundles multiple items.

questions.stem: When building multiple catalog items, which components would you evaluate for consolidation and re-use? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When building multiple catalog items, evaluate Sets of Variables (A) and Flows and Subflows (D) for consolidation and reuse. Variable sets can be shared across items to avoid recreating the same fields. Subflows encapsulate reusable fulfillment logic. Entitlements (B) and Icons (C) are not components typically consolidated for reuse across catalog items.

questions.stem: Which record type would you use for a Computer request?
questions.explanation: A Catalog Item (B) is the correct record type for a Computer request. Catalog Items generate Requested Items and Catalog Tasks for fulfillment of standard goods and services. Record Producer (A) creates records in other tables like Incident. Content Item (C) is informational. Order Guide (D) bundles multiple items — a single computer request doesn't require an Order Guide.

questions.stem: What are the different ways a user can locate items in a service catalog? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use the search on catalog or portal
Use the Top Request or Popular Items widget

questions.explanation: Users can locate catalog items by: using the search on catalog or portal (A) to find items by keyword, and navigating through the categories (B) to browse the catalog hierarchy. Top Request/Popular Items (C) widgets display frequently ordered items but aren't a navigation method users control. Application navigator (D) is for platform navigation, not catalog browsing.

questions.stem: Your customer complains that when their users click on the Configuration Item magnifier from the Incident form, that they are overwhelmed by the volume of CIs to choose from. They want to exclude certain types of CIs from the CI lists on the Incident. Problem and Change forms. What do you recommend to your customer?

options.text: Add a Show field to the base cmdb table: Check the Show box on those CI records they want to display; make reference qualifier to display only the CIs with show=true
Use the Principal CI class checkbox, to identify the CI classes that they want visible on the Incident, Problem, and Change forms
Create an Access control to hide the unnecessary CIs from the itil users
Make a show/hide UI action to show only the desired CIs to the itil users

questions.explanation: Use the Principal CI class checkbox (B) to identify which CI classes should be visible on Incident, Problem, and Change forms. Only CI classes with Principal CI checked appear in the CI reference field lookup. This provides a clean, maintained way to filter CI types without custom qualifiers (A), ACLs (C), or UI actions (D). It's the baseline approach designed for this exact scenario.

questions.stem: Incidents are stored in what table?
questions.explanation: Incidents are stored in the Incident [incident] table (B). The table name is 'incident' and the display label is 'Incident'. Options A (sn_task_incident), C (task_incident), and D (sn_incident) are not valid ServiceNow table names for the incident table.

questions.stem:
Incidents can be created and managed in the workspace, using UI layouts that are tailored to different personas, processes, and interfaces. Examples include:

• Default
• Major incidents
• Self Service
• Mobile

What are these UI layouts called in the Now Platform?
questions.explanation: Views (E) are the UI layouts tailored to different personas, processes, and interfaces. Examples include Default, Major Incidents, Self Service, and Mobile views. Views control which fields appear and how the form is organized for each context. Form Layouts (A), Workspaces (B), Forms (C), and Form Designs (D) are related concepts but Views is the specific term for these persona-specific layouts.

questions.stem: The Major Incident Management (MIM) application is linked to the Incident management process, but the records have an additional set of States. What are these MI States?

options.text: New, Work in progress, Escalated, Communicated

questions.explanation: Major Incident Management (MIM) states are: Proposed, Accepted, Rejected, Cancelled (A). An incident is proposed as a Major Incident, then either Accepted (becoming active MI) or Rejected. Accepted MIs can be Cancelled. There is no Reopened (B), eCAB Convened (C), or Escalated/Communicated (D) states in the MIM process. These states control the MI lifecycle separate from the incident state field.

questions.stem: What would you use to create Incident records, based on email sent by users or systems?
questions.explanation: Inbound Flow Actions (B) create incident records based on emails sent by users or systems. In the Flow Designer paradigm, inbound email processing uses email triggers and flow actions to parse incoming emails and create/update records. Record Producer (A) is for portal-based submissions. Data Collection Job (C) is for Performance Analytics. Transform Map (D) is for data import, not email processing.

questions.stem: What tools are available to the assignee to help resolve an incident? (Choose two.)
