questions.explanation: Incident assignees can use Knowledge Articles (A) to find documented solutions and Known Errors (B) to find workarounds and root causes from problem management. These are the primary resolution tools for working incidents. CI Class Manager (C) is CMDB administration. Enterprise CMDB Dashboard (D) monitors CMDB health. Incident Overview Dashboard (E) is for management reporting.

questions.stem: When you activate the ITSM Roles plugin, what additional granular roles are created for the Incident application? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The ITSM Roles plugin creates sn_incident_read (B) for view-only access and sn_incident_write (C) for edit access to incidents. These granular roles supplement the base itil role. sn_incident_update (A) and sn_incident_insert (D) are not the actual role names created by the plugin — the plugin uses the read/write naming convention.

questions.stem: What are some good practices for guiding your customers' use of Notifications? (Choose three.)

options.text: Make sure Notification requirements and test plans are in the project scope from the start
Get input from Marketing department, regarding format of customer/caller facing notifications
Use templates to ensure consistency and ease of configuration
Use incident.itil.role template as the master template to build all other ITSM templates
When possible, maximize the quantity of email updates to customers

questions.explanation: Good notification practices: ensure requirements and test plans are in project scope from the start (A), get Marketing input for customer-facing notification formatting (B), and use templates for consistency and easy configuration (C). Using incident.itil.role as a master template (D) is too specific and not best practice. Maximizing email quantity (E) leads to notification fatigue — minimize, don't maximize.

questions.stem: Your customer wants to use Incident Tasks on Incident records. But for efficiency reasons, they want to automatically close all Incident Tasks when the parent Incident is closed or canceled. How could you meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

options.text: On Incident Properties, for Autoclose Incident Tasks, select Yes
On Incident Properties, for Close open Incident Tasks when Incident is closed or canceled, select Yes

questions.explanation: To auto-close incident tasks when the parent incident closes: from Incident Properties, enable 'Close open Incident Tasks when Incident is closed or canceled' (C), and enable the system property com.snc.incident.incident_task.closure (D). Autoclose Incident Tasks (A) is not the exact property name. The resolved_at property (B) relates to incident auto-closure, not task closure.

questions.stem: Incident management includes limited functionality for what advanced reporting capability?
questions.explanation: Incident management includes limited Performance Analytics (B) functionality for advanced reporting. PA provides trending, KPI tracking, and predictive analytics beyond standard reports. Analytics Dashboards (A) is too vague. Machine Learning Metrics (C) is not a standard reporting feature name. KPI Reports (D) are part of PA, not a separate capability.

questions.stem: Your client indicates they would like a way to designate VIP callers on an incident form. How would you accomplish this?
questions.explanation: A VIP Flag field style (C) visually highlights VIP callers on the incident form by applying a distinctive visual treatment (like a gold border or icon) to the caller field when the user is flagged as VIP. Dictionary entry (A) defines field properties. Flash action script (B) is not standard. Reference decorator (D) adds icons to reference fields but isn't the VIP-specific mechanism.

questions.stem: What happens if an agent hovers over the reference icon next to the caller field on an incident record and there is not a sys_popup view defined for the [sys_user] table?

options.text: The default view of the User form is displayed
Only dot-walked fields will be displayed
There will be no reference icon if there is no sys_popup defined

questions.explanation: If no sys_popup view is defined for the sys_user table, hovering over the reference icon displays the default view of the User form (A). The system falls back to the default view when no popup-specific view exists. No error is displayed (B). It's not limited to dot-walked fields (C). The reference icon still appears regardless of whether sys_popup is defined (D).

questions.stem: If the Assignment group is empty on an incident record, what happens when an agent that is a member of multiple user groups clicks the Assign to me UI action?

options.text: An error is displayed indicating the agent must manually assign the incident
The agent is prompted to select the Assignment group
The Assignment group field automatically populates with the agent's primary group
The Assignment group field will not populate

questions.explanation: When an agent belongs to multiple groups and the Assignment group is empty, clicking 'Assign to me' prompts the agent to select which Assignment group to use (B). The system can't automatically determine the correct group from multiple options. No error is displayed (A). Primary group isn't auto-selected (C) because the system requires explicit selection. The field doesn't remain empty (D).

questions.stem: Where are the timeframe conditions for sending an SLA breach warning notification defined?
questions.explanation: The timeframe conditions for SLA breach warning notifications are defined in the Default SLA flow (B). The flow contains the timing logic for when warning notifications fire (e.g., at 50% or 75% of the SLA duration). SLA definition records (A) define the SLA parameters. SLA Properties (C) manages global SLA settings. SLA trigger conditions (D) is not where warning timing is configured.

questions.stem: Your customer wants to give secure access to business users to view problem records and reports for the products they support. When you install the ITSM roles plugin, what additional problem role is installed to support this requirement?
questions.explanation: The ITSM Roles plugin installs the sn_problem_read role (B) which gives business users secure, read-only access to view problem records and reports. This role is designed for users who need visibility into problem management activities without the ability to modify records. sn_business_user (A), sn_service_owner (C), sn_problem_write (D), and sn_problem_business_user (E) are not the correct role name for read-only access.

questions.stem:
A new Problem Coordinator accidentally created several problem investigations that need to be deleted.

What role is required to delete a problem record?
questions.explanation: The problem_admin role (D) is required to delete problem records. Problem admins have full administrative control including the ability to delete. sn_problem_delete (A) is not a real role. itil_manager (B) doesn't have delete rights. problem_manager (C) can manage problem lifecycle but not delete records. problem_coordinator (E) manages assignments and communication but cannot delete.

questions.stem:
A tester has submitted a bug report, because at no point in the Problem lifecycle, does the Create Known Error article link appear under Related Links. Also, they notice there is no Known Error knowledge base in the instance.

What might be the cause of this?

options.text: The Problem Management Best Practice - Madrid - Knowledge Integration plugin has not been activated
The customer did not pay the bill for Knowledge management
Tester is not impersonating Problem Coordinator
The sn_known_error_write role is required to see the Create Known Error article link
The requirement was not in the stories

questions.explanation: The Problem Management Best Practice - Madrid - Knowledge Integration plugin (A) needs to be activated for the Known Error functionality to work. Without this plugin, the Known Error knowledge base isn't created and the Create Known Error article link doesn't appear. Cost (B) doesn't affect plugin availability. The role (C, D) issue is secondary to the plugin not being activated. Requirements (E) is not the issue.

questions.stem:
A new problem manager wants a high level view of the activities in problem management.

What module do you recommend?
questions.explanation: Problem > Overview (B) provides a high-level view of problem management activities including open problems by priority, recent activity, and key metrics. It's designed for managers to quickly assess the state of problem management. Problem > Homepage (A) is the older format. ITIL Manager Homepage (C) is broader. Process Health Dashboard (D) and Dashboard (E) are not the standard module names for this overview.

questions.stem: Why don't Problem records automatically move from Resolved to Closed after the fix is implemented?

options.text: It is designed to follow the ITIL4 standard
There is a scheduled job that automatically moves Resolved problems to Closed after 7 days
There is no Closed state. Problem records are moved to Completed
It is good practice to monitor fixes implemented, to ensure the underlying issues are resolved, before closing a problem record

questions.explanation: Problem records don't automatically move from Resolved to Closed because it's good practice to monitor implemented fixes to ensure underlying issues are truly resolved before closing (D). This verification period confirms the fix is effective and no regression occurs. It's not an ITIL4 standard requirement (A). There's no 7-day auto-close job for problems (B). The Closed state exists for problems (C).

questions.stem:
In the life of a Problem record, there are opportunities to click the Re-Analyze button and move backwards in the lifecycle.

When you click the Re-Analyze button, what state is set on the problem record?
questions.explanation: Clicking the Re-Analyze button sets the problem record state to Root Cause Analysis (C). This moves the problem back to the investigation phase so the team can re-examine the root cause. It doesn't go to Assess (A), which is the initial evaluation state. Draft (B) isn't a standard problem state for re-analysis. Fix in Progress (D) is a forward state, not a re-analysis state.

questions.stem:
The key stakeholder for your ITSM implementation wants to have SLAs on every Task record.

What advice do you give regarding SLAs on Problem records?

options.text: SLAs are essential to problem management, as support specialists need to quickly identify root causes
SLAs may be counterproductive to problem management, as the key objective is to permanently fix an error no matter how long that may take
SLAs are available for problem management, but require custom code
SLAs are recommended in the ITIL framework for problem management

questions.explanation: SLAs may be counterproductive to problem management because the key objective is to permanently fix an error regardless of how long it takes (B). Rushing root cause analysis to meet SLA targets can lead to incomplete fixes and recurring issues. SLAs aren't essential for problems (A). They don't require custom code (C). ITIL doesn't specifically recommend SLAs for problem management (D).

questions.stem: What are two effective measures of performance for the Problem Management process? (Choose two.)

options.text: Problems older than 30 days by Priority and State
Number of Problem that have Breached SLAs
Percentage of Problem Resolution within SLA by Category

questions.explanation: Effective Problem Management KPIs: Problems older than 30 days by Priority and State (A) tracks aging problems indicating investigation delays, and Average Problem Resolution Time (D) measures efficiency of the problem management process. SLA-based metrics (B, C) are less relevant for problem management since SLAs can be counterproductive to thorough root cause analysis, as covered in best practices.

questions.stem:
Your customer has an external system, which is used to perform changes. Your customer wants to capture these changes in your instance for reporting and CMDB maintenance purposes.

What baseline Change Model supports this scenario?
questions.explanation: The Change Registration model (D) supports capturing changes performed in external systems for reporting and CMDB maintenance purposes. It's a lightweight model for registering changes that don't go through the full ServiceNow change workflow. Cloud Infrastructure (A) is for cloud changes. Automated Changes (B) is for automated processes. Retroactive Changes (C) is not a baseline model. Unauthorized Changes (E) are detected, not planned.

questions.stem: Where are the technical approvals defined, that are executed in the Change - Normal - Assess flow?
questions.explanation: Technical approvals in the Change - Normal - Assess flow are defined in the Change Approval Policy (A). The Approval Policy contains conditions and decisions that determine which approvals are required based on change attributes. Change Assess Approval Subflow (B) is not the correct name. Change Approval Matrix (C) is not the Quebec+ approach. Change Approval Subflow (D) is too generic.

questions.stem: What is the trigger for the Change - Normal - Assess Flow?

options.text: A Change request using the Normal Change model is moved to the Assess state
A Change request using the Normal Change model is created
A Change request using the Normal Change model is Low Risk, and is moved to the Assess state
A Change request using the Normal Change model is Assigned to a group

questions.explanation: The Change - Normal - Assess flow triggers when a change request using the Normal Change model is moved to the Assess state (A). The flow activates specifically on this state transition, not on creation (B), only for low risk (C), or on group assignment (D). Each flow in the Normal model is tied to a specific state transition.

questions.stem:
A CAB manager is looking for a way to make their CAB meetings more organized and efficient. They want to be able to:

• Define CAB meeting agendas
• View change calendars
• Review, Approve or Reject changes directly from the change application

What feature would you recommend?
questions.explanation: The CAB Workbench (E) provides capabilities to define meeting agendas, view change calendars, and review/approve/reject changes directly from the change application. It's the comprehensive tool for CAB meeting management. Change CAB Dashboard (A), CMDB Health Dashboard (B), CAB Taskboard (C), and Change Overview (D) don't provide the full range of CAB meeting management capabilities.

questions.stem: What are the Release types available on the baseline release record?

options.text: Major, Minor, Upgrade, Emergency, Maintenance, Patch
Alpha, Beta, Snapshot, Nightly, Milestone, Release Candidate

questions.explanation: The baseline Release types are: Major, Minor, Upgrade, Emergency, Maintenance, Patch (B). These cover the full spectrum from large releases to small patches. Standard/Normal/Emergency (A, C) are Change types, not Release types. Alpha/Beta/Snapshot/Nightly (D) are software build nomenclature, not ServiceNow Release Management types.

questions.stem: On a Normal Change Model, what are some examples of the Model State Transitions that are defined for the Authorize state?

options.text: Authorize to Draft, Authorize to Assess, Authorize to Review
Authorize to Implement, Authorize to Assess, Authorize to Review
Authorize to Canceled, Authorize to New, Authorize to Scheduled
Authorize to Scheduled, Authorize to Closed, Authorize to New

questions.explanation: Model State Transitions for the Authorize state include: Authorize to Canceled (for abandoning the change), Authorize to New (returning for rework), and Authorize to Scheduled (progressing to scheduled implementation) (C). Authorize doesn't go to Draft or Assess directly (A). Going from Authorize to Implement skips Scheduled (B). Authorize to Closed isn't a valid transition — changes must be implemented or canceled first (D).

questions.stem: What are the components of a Flow Action?
questions.explanation: A Flow Action consists of Inputs (parameters received), Action Steps (the operations performed), and Outputs (data returned) (C). This Input→Process→Output structure defines how each action works within a flow. Processes/Subprocesses (A, B) aren't Flow Action terminology. Indexes (D) are database concepts, not flow components.

questions.stem: What are key relationships between Change and Release Management? (Choose three.)

options.text: Release management application is required, to use the Change management application
Change includes planning and approvals; Release includes building, testing and execution of changes
A Release can contain one or more Changes
A Change can contain one or more Releases
Change management provides governance, which includes Release management

questions.explanation: Key Change-Release relationships: Change handles planning and approvals while Release handles building, testing, and execution (B); a Release can contain one or more Changes (C); and Change management governance includes Release management (E). Release isn't required for Change (A) — they're independent applications. A Change doesn't contain Releases (D) — it's the reverse relationship.

questions.stem: In release management, what controls the movement of the state from Scoping to Awaiting Approval?
questions.explanation: In Release Management, the movement from Scoping to Awaiting Approval is controlled by manual state selection (A). Unlike Change Management which uses flows and state transition models, Release Management relies on users manually advancing the state. Workflow (B), State model (C), and Flow (D) don't control release state transitions — release states are manually managed.

questions.stem: What are key relationships between Changes and Incidents? (Choose two.)

options.text: Incidents autoclose upon closure of a related Change
Incidents can be caused by a Change
Incident owners are part of the change approval workflow

questions.explanation: Key relationships between Changes and Incidents: Incidents can be caused by a Change (B) — a failed change may create incidents, and a Change can resolve Incidents (C) — implementing a change may fix the root cause of incidents. Incidents don't autoclose on change closure (A). Incident owners aren't part of the change approval workflow (D) by default.

questions.stem: What are key relationships between Change and Problem records? (Choose two.)

options.text: Changes which cause Incidents, should have an associated Problem
A Problem can be solved by a Change
A Change can cause a Problem
A Problem must be associated with a Change, before it can be closed

questions.explanation: Key relationships between Change and Problem: a Problem can be solved by a Change (B) — implementing a change fixes the underlying issue, and a Change can cause a Problem (C) — a change may introduce new issues that generate problems. Changes causing incidents needing problems (A) isn't a direct Change-Problem relationship. Problems don't require an associated Change to close (D).

questions.stem:
You have just released a new Change Model to the testers. Testers report they can see the old change models, but cannot see the new change model on the change landing page.

What could cause this?

options.text: Testers need itil role to see the change models
New change model needs Active to be set to True
New change models are only visible to Change Managers

questions.explanation: The new change model needs its Active field set to True (B) to appear on the change landing page. Inactive models are hidden from the selection list. The itil role (A) should already provide visibility for active models. New models aren't restricted to Change Managers only (C). Workflow publication (D) isn't required for the model to appear — the Active flag controls visibility.

questions.stem: How are Features related to Products and Releases?

options.text: Emergency releases can include products and features
Products have associated features, which are organized into releases
Features are included in releases, not associated with products
Products use features to define release types

questions.explanation: Products have associated features, which are organized into releases (B). In Release Management, products define what you deliver, features are the capabilities of products, and releases group features for coordinated deployment. Emergency releases don't specifically include products (A). Features ARE associated with products (C is wrong). Products don't use features to define release types (D).

questions.stem: When a Service Desk again shares a "How to" item with a customer, what type of record is being shared?
questions.explanation: When a Service Desk agent shares a 'How to' item with a customer, they're sharing a Knowledge article (A). Knowledge articles include 'How to' content that provides step-by-step instructions for common tasks. Content object (B), Information item (C), and How to document (D) are not standard ServiceNow record types for this purpose.

questions.stem: What are the different ways a user can provide feedback on a knowledge article? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Users can provide feedback on knowledge articles via: Helpful? (A) for yes/no usefulness rating, Flag Article (B) to report issues, 5-star scale (C) for quality rating, and Comment on Article (E) for written feedback. 10-star scale (D) is not available — only 5-star. Pin Article (F) is a personal organization feature, not a feedback mechanism.

questions.stem: Where should an admin go to view all of the search queries entered by users in the knowledge search?
questions.explanation: The Search logs application (D) is where administrators view all search queries entered by users in knowledge search. It logs search terms, timestamps, and result counts to help identify gaps in knowledge base content. Knowledge queries application (A) is not a standard module. kb_view (B) tracks article views. kb_feedback (C) stores user feedback on articles, not search queries.

questions.stem: Which of the following catalog client script methods will modify the choice list options available to an end user on a catalog item?
questions.explanation: Catalog client scripts have types: onChange, onLoad, and onSubmit. The onLoad type fires when the catalog item form first loads, which is when you can modify the choice list options available to the end user using g_form.removeOption() or g_form.addOption(). onChange fires on field value changes and onSubmit fires on form submission — neither is the right time to initially modify choice lists.

questions.stem: Which property on an order guide will pass variables from one item to another item with equivalent variables?
questions.explanation: The 'Cascade Variables' property on an Order Guide passes variable values from one catalog item to another item that has equivalent (matching) variables. When cascade is enabled, if Item A sets a variable and Item B has a variable with the same name, Item B automatically inherits the value. This streamlines the ordering process by avoiding redundant data entry across items in the guide.

questions.stem:
ServiceNow contains a resource with information about all services. It is used to support the sale and delivery of services to employees and customers. It includes information about deliverables, options, prices, delivery and performance targets.

What is this resource called?
questions.explanation: The Service Catalog is the ServiceNow resource containing information about all services, supporting the sale and delivery of services to employees and customers. It includes deliverables, options, prices, delivery targets, and performance targets. Service Portal is an end-user interface, Service Map visualizes CI relationships, and Service Dashboard is for analytics — none of these comprehensively stores service information for delivery.

questions.stem: The ability to authorize requests is enabled using a role which requires a user license. What is this role?
questions.explanation: The approver_user role is required to authorize requests in ServiceNow. This role requires a user license (not a fulfiller license) and grants the ability to approve or reject approval records. The other options are not standard OOB roles for request authorization — ServiceNow uses approver_user as the baseline role for approval capabilities.

questions.stem: Released in Quebec, what tool enables the creation of templates for Catalog Items?
questions.explanation: Catalog Builder was released in the Quebec release as a tool for creating templates for Catalog Items and Record Producers. It provides a guided, no-code experience for building catalog items with variables, flows, and approval definitions. Template Builder (A), Catalog Wizard (B), Catalog Template Library (C), and Template Management (E) are not actual ServiceNow tools for catalog item creation.

questions.stem:
Your customer would like to add a field to the Something is Broken record producer form.

Which formatter would you use to add the field?
questions.explanation: The Default Variables Editor is the formatter used to add fields (variables) to a Record Producer form like 'Something is Broken.' It allows administrators to define and arrange the variables that appear on the record producer when end users submit it. Form Designer is for standard form layouts, not record producer variables. The other options are not real ServiceNow tools.

questions.stem: Which record type would you use for a View Company Policies link that would redirect to a Knowledge Article?
questions.explanation: A Content Item is a catalog record type that provides informational links or references without generating a request. A 'View Company Policies' link redirecting to a Knowledge Article is purely informational — it doesn't create a task, request, or record. Record Producers create records, Order Guides bundle multiple items, and Catalog Items generate requested items with fulfillment tasks. Content Items are specifically designed for navigation links and informational content.

questions.stem:
On a request form, the requester needs to indicate when they need to receive the item.

What Variable type would you use for this information?
questions.explanation: The Date variable type is used when the requester needs to indicate a specific calendar date, such as when they need to receive an item. Date provides a date picker for selecting a calendar date. Due Date is not a variable type, Date Picker is the same concept but Date is the correct variable type name, and Duration captures a span of time (hours/minutes) rather than a specific calendar date.

questions.stem: Which type of catalog item may be found in a Service Catalog?
questions.explanation: Content Items are a type of catalog item found in the Service Catalog. They provide informational links and reference content without generating requests. Requested Items (A) are records generated AFTER submitting a catalog item — they're not items in the catalog themselves. Categories (C) organize items but aren't items. Execution Plans (D) define fulfillment steps, not catalog entries.

questions.stem: When a user submits a service request from a catalog, what actions are triggered, based on the flow definition? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: When a user submits a service request from a catalog, the flow definition triggers Tasks (A) for fulfillment work, Notifications (D) to relevant stakeholders, and Approvals (E) for authorization. Access Controls (B) are ACL rules that govern record-level security and are not triggered by flows. Action Specs (C) are not a standard flow component for catalog request processing.

questions.stem: When building out a service catalog, categorizing items helps users navigate and search in the catalog. Which roles would allow you to create and maintain categories? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The roles that allow creating and maintaining service catalog categories are catalog_admin (A), catalog_manager (C), and catalog_editor (D). catalog_admin has full control over catalog configuration. catalog_manager can manage catalog structure including categories. catalog_editor can edit catalog items and categories. itil_admin (B) manages ITSM processes but doesn't specifically manage catalog categories. catalog_builder_editor (E) is for Catalog Builder, not category management.

questions.stem: When defining SLAs for the service catalog, at what level is the SLA typically defined?
questions.explanation: SLAs for the service catalog are typically defined at the Requested Item (RITM) level. Each requested item represents a single catalog item order and tracks its own fulfillment timeline. The Request (REQ) groups multiple RITMs. SLAs at the Request level would be too broad, while Catalog Task level would be too granular. The Service Catalog level doesn't directly support SLA definitions.

questions.stem: What functionality can be used to define the sequence of activities that should be taken to complete catalog items? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Workflows (B) and Flows (D) are the two mechanisms in ServiceNow used to define the sequence of activities for completing catalog items. Workflows (legacy) and Flows (Flow Designer, current) both define approval steps, tasks, notifications, and fulfillment activities. Activity Map (A) is not a real feature. State Transitions (C) manage record state changes but don't define fulfillment activity sequences.

questions.stem:
Your customer wants to limit the users who are able to see internal Network requests, to members of the Network department.

Which roles would enable you to make these required changes? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: To limit catalog item visibility to Network department members, you need user_criteria_admin (B) to create user criteria records that define who can see items, and catalog_admin (C) to apply those criteria to catalog items/categories. catalog_editor (A) can edit items but lacks permissions to manage user criteria restrictions. catalog_manager (D) manages catalog structure but not user criteria configuration.

questions.stem: What should you use to capture data in a grid layout on a catalog item?
questions.explanation: Multi-row variable sets (MRVS) capture data in a grid layout on catalog items. They allow users to enter multiple rows of structured data (like a table/spreadsheet) with defined columns. Regular variable sets (B) group variables but don't create grids. Cascade variables (C) pass values between order guide items. Grid variable (D) is not a standard ServiceNow variable type.

questions.stem: From a data model perspective, which table is the base class for the configuration management database?
questions.explanation: The Base Configuration Item [cmdb] table is the base class for the CMDB from a data model perspective. All CI classes extend from cmdb → cmdb_ci → specific CI classes. The cmdb table is the root ancestor. Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] (A) extends cmdb and is the parent for most CI types but is not the base class. Asset [asset] (B) is a separate hierarchy. Base Item [cmdb_base_item] (C) is not the correct table name.

questions.stem: Which role has the ability to configure and manage Incident Management properties?
questions.explanation: The incident_manager role has the ability to configure and manage Incident Management properties. This role provides administrative capabilities for incident configuration including properties, assignment rules, and incident workflows. The itil role (B) is for general ITSM users. itil_admin (C) manages broader ITSM settings. incident_admin (A) is not a standard OOB role.

questions.stem: Which of the following options can a survey administrator define on an individual survey? (Choose two.)

options.text: The ability for end users to decline survey assignments

questions.explanation: A survey administrator can define Trigger conditions (C) that determine when a survey is sent, and Anonymize responses (D) to protect respondent identity. The ability to decline surveys (A) is a system-level setting, not per-survey. Number of reminder notifications (B) is typically configured at a system/notification level, not as an individual survey administrator option.

questions.stem: How do you define the content that is tracked and displayed in all Incident record activity streams?

options.text: Configure the Activity stream client script
Configure the dictionary entry for the Activity stream
Configure the available fields from the Activity stream filter

questions.explanation: The activity stream filter configuration defines what content is tracked and displayed in incident activity streams. By configuring the available fields from the Activity stream filter (D), you control which field changes, journal entries, and updates appear. Client scripts (A) handle form behavior, form design (B) manages layout, and dictionary entries (C) define field attributes — none directly control activity stream content.

questions.stem: Which table stores incident categories and subcategories?
questions.explanation: The Choice [sys_choice] table stores incident categories and subcategories. ServiceNow uses the sys_choice table to store choice list values for dropdown fields, including Category and Subcategory on the incident table. Category [sys_category] (A) doesn't exist as a standard table for this purpose. Task Category (B) is not the correct table. The Incident table (D) stores incident records, not the category definitions themselves.

questions.stem: What is normally done when a Root Cause and a Workaround are identified for a problem to document the quickest known resolution?
questions.explanation: When a root cause and workaround are identified for a problem, you document a Known Error to record the quickest known resolution. A Known Error article documents the root cause AND the workaround so that service desk agents can quickly resolve related incidents. Publishing a workaround (A) communicates the temporary fix but doesn't create the formal known error record. Completing investigation (C) or RCA (D) are process steps, not documentation actions.

questions.stem:
Your customer wants Problem records to be assigned automatically to the Support group associated with the CI on the problem record.

Which business rule already satisfies this requirement?

options.text: Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO
Populate Assignment Group based on Cl Support Group
Problem Assignment Group based on CI Support Group

questions.explanation: The OOB business rule 'Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO' automatically assigns the support group associated with the CI on a problem record to the Assignment Group field. This rule checks the CI's support group and, if available, the Service Offering's support group. The other options are not standard OOB business rule names in ServiceNow Problem Management.

questions.stem:
Your customer wants to change the way Priority on Problem records is calculated based on Impact and Urgency.

Which module should you use to locate and update the Priority Problem Lookup record?
questions.explanation: Data Lookup Definitions is where you locate and update the Priority Problem Lookup record to change how Priority is calculated from Impact and Urgency. ServiceNow uses data lookup rules to map Impact/Urgency combinations to Priority values. Priority Matrix (A) is the conceptual model. Choice Lists (B) store field values. Priority Rule Definitions (D) is not the correct module name for this configuration.

questions.stem:
The current status of a problem record is tracked in the State field. Each state has a label, value and constant. This example is for Fix in Progress state:


Label: Fix in Progress -

Value: 104 -
Constant Problem State STATES.FIX IN PROGRESS

Your customer wants to add a prerequisite for moving out of the Fix in Progress state. When you update the script include which value is better to use in the script?
questions.explanation: When writing scripts, you should use the constant ProblemState.STATES.FIX_IN_PROGRESS rather than the numeric value 104 or the label string. Constants are self-documenting, immune to value changes across upgrades, and easier to maintain. Using raw values (A) makes code fragile if ServiceNow changes numbering. String labels (B) break if renamed. Option D is not valid syntax.

questions.stem:
A problem investigation had been previously closed, because the risk was accepted, in favor of using the workaround, instead of applying the fix. After a couple of weeks, the issue starts to occur more frequently, so management wants to re-visit the root cause analysis.

What would be the next step for this problem?

options.text: If 7 days has passed, since the Problem was closed, it cannot be re-opened
Problem Manager clicks Re-Analyze on the Problem record
Problem Assignee clicks Re-Open on the Problem record
Administrator clicks Re-Open on the Problem Record

questions.explanation: When a previously closed problem needs to be revisited, the Problem Manager clicks 'Re-Analyze' on the Problem record. Re-Analyze reopens the investigation and moves the problem back to a Root Cause Analysis state for further work. There is no 7-day limitation on reopening (A). 'Re-Open' is not the correct button name (C, D) — ServiceNow uses 'Re-Analyze' specifically for returning closed problems to investigation.

questions.stem: Which baseline Change Flow automatically generates a Change task, for Post Implementation Review?
questions.explanation: The 'Change - Emergency - Review' flow automatically generates a Change Task for Post Implementation Review (PIR). In the emergency change lifecycle, when the change reaches the Review state, this flow creates a PIR task to evaluate whether the emergency change was successful. The Authorize flows (B, D) handle approval, not review tasks. Options C and E are not standard OOB flow names.

questions.stem:
Your customer wants to use the Normal change model, but wants to add another level of approval for changes relating to the Service, SAP Enterprise Services.

What should you do to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Add a new Policy Input to the Normal Change Approval Policy
Add a new Decision to the Normal Change Approval Policy
Add a new Change Approval Policy
Add a new Decision to the Normal Change Workflow

questions.explanation: To add another level of approval for changes relating to SAP Enterprise Services within the Normal change model, you should add a new Decision to the Normal Change Approval Policy. Decisions within an approval policy define conditions and the resulting approval requirements. Adding a Policy Input (A) modifies what data the policy evaluates. Creating a new policy (C) is overkill for a single service exception. Editing the workflow (D) is a legacy approach.

questions.stem: What actions can a user with the itil_admin role take in support of Change Management? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The itil_admin role in Change Management can: Manage Risk Assessments (A), Manage Risk Conditions (C), and Delete Change (D). itil_admin has elevated ITSM administrative capabilities including risk management and record deletion. Deleting a CAB Definition (B) typically requires change_admin. Creating and managing Approval Policies (E) requires the change_manager role, not itil_admin.

questions.stem:
You have just upgraded your instance and have not migrated to multimodal change.

Using the default settings, when you click on Change > Create new, what page displays?
questions.explanation: When you haven't migrated to multimodal change, clicking Change > Create New displays the Change Interceptor page by default. The interceptor prompts the user to select the change type (Normal, Standard, Emergency) before creating the record. The Change Landing Page (C) is the multimodal experience. The Change Form (B) appears after type selection. Change Overview (D) is not the page displayed for creation.

questions.stem: What is an example of a Key Performance Indicator for Change management that is included with Performance Analytics, but not available in ServiceNow reporting? (Choose two.)

options.text: Count of Completed Changes per Month, by Change Type
Count of Completed Changes per Month, by Category

questions.explanation: Performance Analytics provides KPIs not available in standard ServiceNow reporting, including '% Successful Changes' (A) and '% Unauthorized Changes' (C). These percentage-based KPIs require PA's indicator framework for trending and benchmarking. Count-based metrics like completed changes per month by type (B) or category (D) can be created with standard list reports and don't require PA.

questions.stem: Your customer wants to add a notification to the Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow. What is the first thing you would do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Create a copy of the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow, and then edit the new copy
Create a backup of the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow, and edit the baseline flow
Deactivate the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow
Unpublish the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow

questions.explanation: When modifying a baseline flow, best practice is to first create a copy of the baseline flow and then edit the copy. This preserves the original for reference and rollback. Editing the baseline directly (B) risks losing OOB functionality on upgrades. Deactivating (C) or unpublishing (D) the baseline would disrupt existing change processing before the modification is ready.

questions.stem: In Change Management, what does a Model State contain? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: A Change Model State contains Model State Transitions (D), which define allowed state movements, and Model State Transition Conditions (A), which define the requirements that must be met for each transition. This was confirmed in the ServiceNow docs: model states have hierarchical transitions, and each transition has conditions (Mandatory Fields, Transition Conditions, scripts). Properties (B) and policies (C) are not components of a Model State.

questions.stem: At which level can the type of knowledge feedback be enabled or disabled?
questions.explanation: Knowledge feedback types (Helpful/Unhelpful, Flagging, Comments) can be enabled or disabled at the Knowledge Base level. Each knowledge base has settings controlling which feedback mechanisms are available for its articles. Individual articles (B), categories (C), and templates (D) don't have granular feedback-type configuration — it's managed at the knowledge base level.

questions.stem:
A customer wants to add a new Catalog Item to the Service Catalog.

What process would be used to ensure the new item is authorized?
questions.explanation: Adding a new Catalog Item to the Service Catalog should go through Change Management (D) to ensure the item is properly authorized before being made available. Change Management provides the governance framework for authorizing changes to IT services, including new catalog offerings. Fulfillment (A) handles post-request delivery. Release (B) manages software releases. Configuration (C) tracks CIs. Catalog Management (E) is not a formal ITIL authorization process.

questions.stem: Which of the following cannot be defined or set through a Catalog UI Policy?

options.text: Apply a requirement to all form views
Reverse UI Policy if conditions are false

questions.explanation: A Catalog UI Policy cannot apply a requirement to all form views — it applies only to the catalog form context. Catalog UI Policies can set variables to mandatory (B), reverse if conditions are false (C), and set variables to read-only (D). Unlike standard UI Policies which can apply to specific or all form views, catalog UI policies operate in the service catalog context and don't have the 'Apply to all views' capability.

questions.stem: When configuring stages in Flow Designer, what are some of the options that can be done? (Choose two.)

options.text: Stage labels and names can be changed
States for the requested item records can be renamed
Define a Service Level Agreement for a stage

questions.explanation: When configuring stages in Flow Designer, stage labels and names can be changed (A) to match your process terminology, and estimated durations can be set (D) to provide time expectations for each stage. Stage configuration does not allow renaming request item states (B) — those are system-level. SLA definitions (C) are configured separately in Service Level Management, not within Flow Designer stage configuration.

questions.stem: How are Service Catalogs and Catalog Items related? (Choose two.)

options.text: A catalog item can be associated with one or more service catalogs
Access to catalog items is determined by the service catalog's assigned user criteria
Service catalogs may contain multiple catalog items
A catalog item can only be associated with one service catalog

questions.explanation: A catalog item can be associated with one or more service catalogs (A) through the Catalogs field, and service catalogs may contain multiple catalog items (C). These are the two correct relationships. Option D contradicts A — items CAN belong to multiple catalogs. Option B is incorrect — access to items is controlled by user criteria on the items and categories themselves, not the catalog's user criteria.

questions.stem: Which role has the ability to modify the cart layout?
questions.explanation: The catalog_admin role has the ability to modify the cart layout in ServiceNow. Cart layout configuration, including the checkout experience and cart display options, requires catalog_admin privileges. The itil role (A) is for general ITSM fulfillment. itil_admin (B) manages ITSM processes. catalog_manager (D) manages catalog structure but lacks cart layout modification capabilities.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements are automatically included in the name of the update set for items published via Catalog Builder? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When items are published via Catalog Builder, the automatically generated update set name includes the item name (B) and a timestamp (E). This naming convention ensures each published update set is uniquely identifiable. The catalog name (A), variables (C), and item author (D) are not automatically included in the update set name.

questions.stem: What would you use to define a common grouping of configuration items such as all web servers in Miami?
questions.explanation: Dynamic CI groups define a common grouping of configuration items based on conditions, such as 'all web servers in Miami.' Unlike static groups, dynamic groups automatically include CIs matching the defined criteria. CI class (A) is a category of CIs, not a grouping mechanism. Dependent groups (B) and CSDM component groups (C) are not standard ServiceNow features for this purpose.

questions.stem: After publishing an Item via Catalog Builder, the associated update set is set to which state?
questions.explanation: After publishing an item via Catalog Builder, the associated update set is automatically set to the Complete state. This indicates the update set is finalized and ready for migration. It's not left In Progress (A) since no further changes are expected. New (C) and Published (D) are not standard update set states in this context.

questions.stem: Which platform role can create service portfolios and taxonomy nodes?
questions.explanation: The portfolio_admin role can create service portfolios and taxonomy nodes in Service Portfolio Management. Per the SPM documentation, Portfolio admins 'set up, create, edit, and delete services and service portfolios' and 'update taxonomy nodes, services, service offerings, and reparent services.' Portfolio viewer (A) can only view. Portfolio editor (D) can edit but not create. Portfolio manager (C) is not a standard SPM role.

questions.stem: Which of these can be associated with a service within the service portfolio taxonomy?
questions.explanation: A leaf node is what can be associated with a service within the service portfolio taxonomy. The SPM taxonomy is hierarchical, and services can only be placed at leaf nodes (the lowest level of the tree). Node layer (A), Node (B), and Node level (C) are either not specific enough or not the correct term — only leaf nodes at the bottom of the taxonomy hierarchy can have services attached.

questions.stem: Which service types can be managed through the scope of Service Portfolio Management? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Service Portfolio Management manages Technical services (B) and Business services (C). These are the two primary service types in SPM aligned with the CSDM framework. Technical services are IT infrastructure-focused and consumed internally, while business services are customer-facing. Application services (A) and Mobile services (D) are not standard SPM-managed service types.

questions.stem: Which is the process responsible for delivering items that have been ordered from a Service Catalog?
questions.explanation: Request Management is the ITIL process responsible for delivering items ordered from a Service Catalog. It manages the end-to-end lifecycle from request submission through fulfillment and closure. Catalog Fulfillment (C) describes the activity but isn't the formal process name. Service Catalog Management (A) focuses on the catalog itself, not delivery. Catalog Workflows (B) and Catalog Item Design (D) are components, not processes.

questions.stem: Where is the definition of what is provided, or not provided, for a service defined?
questions.explanation: Service scope defines what is provided and what is not provided for a service. It establishes the boundaries and expectations of a service offering, clarifying inclusions and exclusions. Vendor service agreements (A) govern external vendor terms. Service contracts (C) are formal agreements. Service limitations (D) is not a standard ServiceNow term for this concept.

questions.stem: When using Catalog Builder, what can be built using templates? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Catalog Builder provides templates for building Catalog Items (B) and Record Producers (E). These are the two record types that Catalog Builder supports with its template-based creation experience. Content Items (A), Knowledge articles (C), and Order Guides (D) are not built using Catalog Builder templates.

questions.stem: If a change model has Write roles AND Can write defined, which users have the ability to modify the change model record? (Choose two.)

options.text: Users that have the Write role(s) OR that match the Can write user criteria
Users that have the Write role(s) AND match the Can write user criteria

questions.explanation: When both Write Roles AND Can Write user criteria are defined on a change model, users must have the Write role(s) AND match the Can write user criteria (E) to modify the model. Users with admin role (B) always have full access regardless of restrictions. The AND logic applies — having just one is insufficient (eliminating C which says OR). itil_admin (A) and sn_change_write (D) don't bypass this combined requirement.

questions.stem: What defines the required approvals and the associated conditions for a change model?
questions.explanation: A change approval policy defines the required approvals and associated conditions for a change model. Approval policies contain decisions that evaluate conditions and determine which approvals are needed. State transitions (B) control allowed state movements. Approval definitions (C) and lifecycle flows (D) are not the correct terms for configuring approval requirements on change models.

questions.stem: Which organizational role is responsible for the overall administrative capabilities of a portfolio?
questions.explanation: The Portfolio Manager is responsible for the overall administrative capabilities of a portfolio. The SPM documentation shows Portfolio admin (the role for portfolio managers) can 'set up, create, edit, and delete services and service portfolios' and 'manage portfolios including related commitments and availability.' Service Manager (A) and Service Owner (D) manage services, not portfolios. Portfolio Owner (C) is a stakeholder but the manager handles administration.

questions.stem: What defines which catalog items, and in what order, are included in an Order Guide?
questions.explanation: Rules define which catalog items are included in an Order Guide and in what order they appear. Each rule specifies a catalog item to include and can set conditions for when that item should appear. The rule's Order field determines the sequence. Order guide templates (A) aren't a feature. Variable sets (C) group variables on items. UI policies (D) control form behavior, not guide composition.

questions.stem: A customer requires incidents to automatically move to a Closed state from Resolved after 7 days. How is this configured? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure the incident lifecycle flow script action
Configure the number of days Resolved incidents automatically close property
Configure the incident lifecycle timeline property
Enable the auto closure of Incidents based on Resolution date property

questions.explanation: Two properties must be configured: (B) the number of days after which Resolved incidents automatically close, and (D) the property that enables auto-closure of incidents based on resolution date. Both are required — you must enable the feature AND set the day count. The lifecycle flow script action (A) and lifecycle timeline property (C) are not the correct configuration points for auto-closure.

questions.stem: On the ‘Create New’ change landing page in Service Operations Workspace, what class label is displayed for the Emergency change model?
questions.explanation: On the 'Create New' change landing page in Service Operations Workspace, the Emergency change model displays with the class label 'Break/fix'. This label communicates the purpose of emergency changes — addressing break/fix scenarios that require immediate action. Unauthorized (A), Default (B), and Out-of-the-box (D) are not the labels used for emergency change models.

questions.stem: Which of these can be defined using step based fulfillment in Catalog Builder? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Catalog Builder's step-based fulfillment allows defining Approvals (A) and Tasks (D). These are the two fulfillment components available in the guided Catalog Builder experience. Subflow triggers (B), Notifications (C), and Payment processing (E) are not configurable through Catalog Builder's step-based fulfillment interface.

questions.stem: Which Service Portfolio Management phase does a service belong to when it is in operational state?
questions.explanation: When a service is in operational state, it belongs to the Catalog phase of Service Portfolio Management. The SPM documentation defines three phases: Pipeline (not yet operational), Catalog (operational and available), and Retired (no longer operational). A service that IS operational is in the Catalog phase. Active (A) is not a phase name. Pipeline (D) is for proposed services.

questions.stem: What is normally done when a Root Cause and a Workaround are identified for a problem to document the quickest known resolution?
questions.explanation: When a root cause and workaround are identified, you document a Known Error to record the quickest known resolution. A Known Error article documents both the root cause and the workaround, helping service desk agents quickly resolve related incidents by deflecting them. Publishing a workaround (A) only shares the temporary fix. Document Five Whys (C) is an investigation technique. Complete Investigation (D) is a process step, not a documentation action.

questions.stem: A Portfolio Manager is primarily concerned with the performance of what hierarchy?

options.text: Portfolio Owner, Service Owner, Catalog Manager
Service Catalog, Catalog item, Requested item
Requested Item, Catalog Task, Task SLA

questions.explanation: A Portfolio Manager is primarily concerned with the performance of the Service Portfolio → Service → Service Offering hierarchy. This is the core SPM data model: portfolios contain services, and services have offerings. Option B lists organizational roles, not a service hierarchy. Option C describes the request catalog flow. Option D covers request fulfillment records. Only A represents the portfolio management hierarchy.

questions.stem: When modifying a Change Flow, a library is available of re-usable components for your flow. What are these components called?
questions.explanation: Flow actions are the reusable components available in the library when modifying a Change Flow in Flow Designer. Actions are pre-built operations (like 'Create Task', 'Ask for Approval', 'Send Email') that can be dragged into flows. Flow activities (A) is not the correct terminology. Attributes (C) and Properties (D) are configuration settings, not reusable flow components.

questions.stem: How is granular read and write access for a specific change model defined?

options.text: Configuring ACL's on the chge_model table
Configuring ACL's on the Create New landing page
Setting Advanced Security to true and applying user criteria

questions.explanation: Granular read and write access for a specific change model is defined by setting Advanced Security to true and applying user criteria. When Advanced Security is enabled on a change model, the Available For, Not Available For, and Can Write tabs appear, allowing administrators to define user criteria for read and write access. ACLs on the table (A, B) affect all models, not specific ones. Change properties (C) are global settings.

questions.stem: Which of the following can leverage user criteria for controlling access?
questions.explanation: Catalog items can leverage user criteria for controlling access. User criteria can be applied to catalog items to define who can view and order them (Available For, Not Available For). Catalog taxonomy (A), topics (B), and variables (D) do not support user criteria. Categories (C) also support user criteria but 'catalog items' (E) is the most direct and primary answer to this question about access control.

questions.stem: Which level are service commitments associated in the service portfolio taxonomy?
questions.explanation: Service commitments are associated at the Node level in the service portfolio taxonomy. Nodes in the taxonomy hierarchy can have commitments attached to them, which then apply to the services categorized under those nodes. Offerings (B) have their own SLA commitments but the taxonomy-level association is at the node. Portfolio (C) is too broad, and Service (D) level commitments are managed separately from the taxonomy.

questions.stem: How are the relationships between services and offerings that are built in Service Portfolio Management transferred to the Configuration Management Database (CMDB)?

options.text: Only parent:child (service:offering) relationships are automatically created in the CMDB
If the service is defined as a business service, the relationships and dependencies will be automatically in the CMDB
All CMDB relationships and dependencies are automatically created upon publishing the service and offerings
Any required CMDB relationships and dependencies must be created manually

questions.explanation: All CMDB relationships and dependencies are automatically created upon publishing the service and offerings. When you publish a service in Service Portfolio Management, the system automatically creates the corresponding CMDB entries including parent-child relationships between services and offerings. Manual creation (D) is not required, and the automatic creation is not limited to just parent-child (A) or business services only (B).

questions.stem: What is the minimum number of offering(s) a service must have to move to the Catalog phase?
questions.explanation: A service must have a minimum of 1 offering to move to the Catalog phase. The service needs at least one service offering defined before it can transition from Pipeline to Catalog status, because the Catalog phase represents operational services available for consumption — which requires at least one offering. 2 (B), 3 (C), and 4 (D) exceed the minimum requirement.

questions.stem: Your client indicates they would like a way to designate VIP callers on an incident form. How would you accomplish this?
questions.explanation: Field styles allow you to visually designate VIP callers on an incident form by applying conditional formatting. A field style can change the appearance of a field (color, icon, bold) based on conditions — for example, highlighting the Caller field when the caller is a VIP. Dictionary entry attributes (A) define field behavior. Reference decorators (B) add icons near reference fields but aren't used for VIP designation. Action scripts (C) modify records.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines the approvals that should be applied to a change request?
questions.explanation: A change approval policy defines the approvals that should be applied to a change request. Approval policies contain decisions with conditions and approval requirements that determine who must approve a change based on its attributes. UI actions (A) are buttons/links. Script includes (C) are reusable server scripts. Business rules (D) run on record operations but aren't the mechanism for defining approval requirements.

questions.stem: What do you use to identify who will have access to particular items in a service catalog?
questions.explanation: User criteria is the mechanism used to identify who will have access to particular items in a service catalog. User criteria records define conditions (based on users, groups, roles, companies, locations, departments) that determine which catalog items and categories are visible to which users. Access criteria (B), User access rules (C), Availability rules (D), and Security rules (E) are not the correct ServiceNow feature names.

questions.stem: Once a Catalog Item has been requested, what mechanism determines the approvals, and tasks that are triggered in the application?
questions.explanation: Flows (Flow Designer) determine the approvals and tasks triggered when a catalog item is requested. The catalog item's Process Engine field points to a flow that defines the fulfillment process including approval steps, task creation, and notifications. Decision Tables (A) evaluate conditions for routing. Actions (B) are components within flows. Run Books (C) are operational procedures. Playbooks (E) guide agents through resolution steps.

questions.stem: What is a core difference between an Incident and a Problem?

options.text: Incidents are focused on one individual having an issue; Problems are when you have many people having the same issue
Incidents can be any priority; Problems are high or critical
Incidents are the same as a Problem
Incidents are focused on the quickest resolution; Problems are focused on root cause analysis

questions.explanation: The core difference is that Incidents are focused on the quickest resolution to restore service, while Problems are focused on root cause analysis to prevent recurrence. Incident Management aims to minimize impact by restoring normal service as quickly as possible. Problem Management investigates underlying causes. Option A incorrectly defines the distinction by number of affected users. Option B incorrectly limits Problem priority. Option C is wrong — they are distinct processes.

questions.stem: Where can a change manager define the fields that must be populated before a change request can move from the state of New to Assess?
questions.explanation: Model State Transition Conditions define the fields that must be populated before a change request can move between states. A change manager configures these conditions on the change model to require specific fields (like Risk, Impact, or Description) before transitioning from New to Assess. Choice conditions (A) and State choice lists (D) don't enforce field requirements. Dictionary Overrides (C) modify field attributes but don't define transition requirements.

questions.stem: When building multiple catalog items, which components should be evaluated for consolidation and re-use? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Flows and Subflows (B) and Sets of variables (C) — known as variable sets — should be evaluated for consolidation and reuse across multiple catalog items. Flows/subflows can be shared across items for common fulfillment processes. Variable sets group commonly needed fields that can be attached to multiple items. Approvals (A) are part of flows, not standalone reusable components. Workflow Triggers (D) are not a reusable catalog component.

questions.stem:
Your company sells bicycles. They want to build a service catalog for current and prospective customers, so they can browse for bicycles and accessories, and make purchases.

What interface is suitable for these external users?
questions.explanation: A Portal (Service Portal) is the suitable interface for external customers to browse and purchase bicycles and accessories. questions.stem: By default, an Assignment group is automatically set on a change request record because of a business rule. How is the group identified?

questions.explanation: By default, the assignment group on a change request is automatically set by a business rule that checks the Support group on the CI record, and if empty, falls back to the Support group on the Service Offering. This OOB behavior populates the Assignment group field based on the configuration item's support group association, using the service offering as a secondary source.

questions.stem: What happens when an existing service record is checked out in service Builder for editing?

options.text: The service portfolio record is placed in a Work in progress state
The service and offerings are temporarily unavailable for consumption
A copy of the service is created and placed in a Draft state
The original service record is placed in a Retired state

questions.explanation: When an existing service record is checked out in Service Builder for editing, a copy of the service is created and placed in a Draft state. questions.stem: Users with which role can Communicate a workaround or fix? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Users with the problem_manager (C) and problem_admin (D) roles can communicate a workaround or fix for a problem. Problem management documentation confirms these two roles have the capability to document and communicate workarounds and fixes. itil_admin (A) manages ITSM settings broadly but doesn't have this specific problem communication capability. problem_task_analyst (B) works on problem tasks, not communication of outcomes.

questions.stem: What tools are available to the assignee to help resolve an incident? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Workarounds (A) and Resolutions from similar incidents (B) are tools available to the assignee to help resolve an incident. The incident form provides access to knowledge articles including workarounds for known errors, and the Similar Incidents feature shows resolutions from previously resolved incidents. CI Class Manager (C) manages CMDB classes. Enterprise CMDB Dashboard (D) is for CMDB analytics. Incident Overview Dashboard (E) is for management reporting.

questions.stem: By default, when using Inbound actions, what happens if an email is received and has an Incident watermark?

options.text: Incident record is set to state = on hold
Incident record is updated, per the action's script
Auto-reply sent to sender, recommending they use Portal chat

questions.explanation: When an inbound email contains an incident watermark, the incident record is updated based on the inbound action's script. The watermark identifies which record the email relates to, and the configured inbound action script processes the email content to update that record (e.g., adding comments, changing state). The record isn't automatically put on hold (A), SLA isn't paused by default (B), and no auto-reply is sent (D).

questions.stem: Which of the following can leverage user criteria for controlling access? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Catalog categories (C) and catalog items (E) can leverage user criteria for controlling access. User criteria defines conditions (users, groups, roles, companies, locations, departments) that determine visibility. Both categories and items have Available For and Not Available For user criteria tabs. Catalog taxonomy (A), topics (B), and variables (D) do not support user criteria for access control.

questions.stem: Which of the following is defined in the Assess Dialog Form View for problem records?

The users that receive notifications when a problem record is moved from the New to Assess state.
The fields which are required to be populated for the record to automatically move from the New to Assess state.

questions.explanation: The Assess Dialog Form View for problem records defines the fields which are required to be populated for the record to automatically move from New to Assess state. When a problem transitions to Assess, this dialog prompts the user to fill in mandatory fields before the transition completes. It doesn't configure notifications (A, C) or dialog text (B) — it enforces required field population for the state transition.

questions.stem: What role is required to accept a Major Incident?
questions.explanation: The major_incident_manager role is required to accept a Major Incident. This specialized role grants the ability to promote incidents to major incident status and manage the major incident process. incident_admin (A) is not a standard OOB role. itil_admin (B) has broad ITSM admin access but not the specific major incident acceptance capability. incident_manager (C) manages incidents generally but cannot accept major incidents without the dedicated role.

questions.stem: Which service type is published to service owners and typically only consumed internally?
questions.explanation: Technical services are published to service owners and typically only consumed internally. In the SPM framework, technical services represent IT infrastructure and platform capabilities used internally by the organization, as opposed to business services which are customer-facing. Mobile services (C) and Application services (D) are not standard SPM service type classifications.

questions.stem: How is granular read and write access for a specific change model defined?

questions.explanation: Granular read and write access for a specific change model is defined by setting Advanced Security to true and applying user criteria. With Advanced Security enabled, Available For, Not Available For, and Can Write tabs appear on the change model, allowing precise control over who can read and write to that specific model. ACLs on the landing page (A) or table (C) affect all models. Change properties (D) are global settings.

questions.stem: In what part of the Request management lifecycle, does the user fill out the form for the item they are requesting?
questions.explanation: The Input phase of the Request Management lifecycle is when the user fills out the form for the item they are requesting. During Input, the user provides the required information (variables) on the catalog item form. Submittal (A) is when the request is formally submitted. Inquiry (B) is when the user browses. Specification (C) is not a standard lifecycle phase. Check out (D) is when the cart is finalized before submission.
